nodes.name: grammar.rs
nodes.summary: Core tree-sitter grammar infrastructure: the Grammar struct holding a parsed ts_language plus all compiled query configs (highlights, brackets, indents, outline, injections, overrides, redactions, runnables, text objects, debug variables), with builder methods that compile each .scm query and resolve capture indices.
nodes.languageNotes: Each with_*_query method wraps a fallible tree-sitter Query::new and validates that required captures are present via populate_capture_indices; grammar ids are handed out from a global atomic counter. This is the central extension surface for adding language grammar features (LaTeX, markdown injections, Jupyter cells) in the fork.

nodes.name: Grammar
nodes.summary: Aggregate holding a compiled tree-sitter language and every optional query config; exposes highlight-map access, highlight_id_for_name lookup, and the with_queries pipeline that compiles a LanguageQueries bundle into config structs.

nodes.name: populate_capture_indices
nodes.summary: Helper that scans a compiled query's capture names, marks required vs optional captures against expected prefixes, and errors if any required capture is missing — the shared validation used by every query builder.

nodes.name: with_queries
nodes.summary: Compiles a full LanguageQueries bundle into the Grammar by dispatching each present query source to its dedicated with_*_query builder, attaching contextual error messages per query type.

nodes.name: with_override_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the scope-override query, mapping capture names to override entries, wiring per-scope opt-in language servers, and reconciling bracket-disabled scopes into override configs.

nodes.name: with_injection_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the injection query used to embed sub-languages (e.g. code blocks in markdown), extracting content/language capture indices and per-pattern injection language and combined settings.

nodes.name: with_outline_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the outline query, resolving required item/name captures and optional context/annotation captures used to build the document symbol outline.

nodes.name: with_indents_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the indentation query, resolving indent/start/end/outdent capture indices and collecting suffixed start captures into a lookup map.

nodes.name: with_brackets_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the brackets query, resolving open/close capture indices and reading per-pattern newline-only and rainbow-exclude property settings.

nodes.name: with_text_object_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the text-object query, mapping each capture name to a TextObject variant (inside/around function, class, comment) for vim-style motions.

nodes.name: with_debug_variables_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the debug-variables query, mapping captures to DebuggerTextObject variable/scope kinds for the debugger's variable inspection.

nodes.name: with_runnable_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the runnables query, classifying captures as Run/RunItem/Named and detecting extra captures plus grouped-runnable support.

nodes.name: with_highlights_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the highlights query and records the identifier capture indices used to distinguish semantic identifiers during highlighting.

nodes.name: with_redaction_query
nodes.summary: Compiles the redaction query, resolving the required redaction capture used to mask sensitive regions during collaboration/screen-sharing.

nodes.name: highlight_map.rs
nodes.summary: Defines HighlightId (a NonZeroU32-backed newtype) and HighlightMap that maps tree-sitter capture indices to theme highlight ids for fast per-capture style lookup.
nodes.languageNotes: HighlightId wraps NonZeroU32 so Option<HighlightId> is niche-optimized to a bare u32.

nodes.name: language_config.rs
nodes.summary: Defines LanguageConfig — the deserializable per-language config schema (name, grammar, matcher, brackets, indent patterns, comments, list configs, soft-wrap, toolchain/LSP opt-ins) — plus supporting config structs and custom serde regex (de)serializers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses custom serde deserialize helpers to compile regex strings into regex::Regex at load time and a hand-written LanguageMatcher ordering that compares regex patterns by their source string. code_fence_block_name and kernel_language_names fields are directly relevant to the fork's markdown/Jupyter goals.

nodes.name: LanguageConfig
nodes.summary: The central per-language configuration struct loaded from a config.toml, carrying grammar name, file matcher, bracket/indent/comment/list rules, soft-wrap, tab settings, and LSP/debugger opt-ins; provides load() and a rich Default.

nodes.name: LanguageMatcher
nodes.summary: Rules for matching a file to a language via path suffixes, a first-line regex, and modeline aliases, with hand-written Ord/PartialOrd/PartialEq that compare regex patterns by source string.

nodes.name: BracketPairConfig
nodes.summary: Holds the configured bracket pairs plus per-bracket disabled scopes, with a custom deserialize that unzips bracket entries from their not_in scope lists and an is_closing_brace helper.

nodes.name: deserialize_regex
nodes.summary: Serde helper that deserializes an optional string field and compiles it into a regex::Regex, surfacing compilation errors as deserialization errors.

nodes.name: language_name.rs
nodes.summary: Defines LanguageName (a SharedString newtype with proto/LSP id conversions) and LanguageId (an atomic-counter-backed unique id), the lightweight identity types threaded through language registration.
nodes.languageNotes: LanguageName implements Borrow<str>, AsRef, Display and From conversions so it interns cheaply and doubles as a hash-map key; lsp_id() lowercases the name and maps empty to 'plaintext'.

nodes.name: LanguageName
nodes.summary: SharedString-backed language name newtype with static/dynamic constructors, proto and LSP id conversions, and Borrow/AsRef/Display trait impls for use as a cheap map key.

nodes.summary: Focusable but non-editable placeholder view used when a picker has no query input editor.

nodes.name: highlighted_match_with_paths.rs
nodes.summary: Renderable components for displaying a fuzzy-matched result with highlighted substrings and optional file path breadcrumbs.

nodes.name: HighlightedMatch
nodes.summary: Renderable text label with highlighted character ranges (from fuzzy match positions) and an optional highlight color.

nodes.name: HighlightedMatchWithPaths
nodes.summary: Renderable combining a highlighted match label with an optional list of path-segment breadcrumbs, used in file/symbol pickers.

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Joins multiple HighlightedMatch segments together with a separator, preserving each segment's highlight positions in the combined range.

nodes.name: parts.rs
nodes.summary: Small shared UI helper rendering a project-scan-in-progress indicator shown in pickers while a workspace scan is running.

nodes.name: project_scan_indicator
nodes.summary: Renders a small spinner/label indicator when the project is still being scanned and the picker has no query yet.

nodes.name: persistence.rs
nodes.summary: Persists and restores a picker's window shape and preview layout preferences across sessions via a key-value store.

nodes.name: PickerConfig
nodes.summary: Serializable width/height/preview-size configuration used to persist and restore a centered picker's shape.

nodes.name: store_shape_for_this_layout
nodes.summary: Saves the current picker shape to persistent storage under a key scoped to the picker delegate and preview layout.

nodes.name: try_load_shape
nodes.summary: Attempts to load a previously persisted picker shape for the given delegate and preview layout from storage.

nodes.name: picker.rs
nodes.summary: Core Picker component and PickerDelegate trait implementing GPUI's generic fuzzy-search picker UI: selection, multi-select, keyboard navigation, query editing, preview layout, and confirmation flows.
nodes.languageNotes: Central generic component parameterized over a PickerDelegate trait that supplies match data and behavior, used throughout the app for command palettes, file finders, and similar list-driven pickers.

nodes.name: Picker
nodes.summary: Generic picker view holding delegate, head, preview, shape, and selection state; renders as either a list or uniform list with optional preview pane.

nodes.name: PickerDelegate
nodes.summary: Trait implemented by picker consumers to supply match count, rendering, filtering, selection, and confirmation behavior for a specific picker instance.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a new Picker with the given delegate, container kind, head, and preview, wiring up initial shape and subscriptions.

nodes.name: set_selected_index
nodes.summary: Updates the picker's selected index, handling multi-select toggling, scroll-to-index behavior, and delegate notification.

nodes.name: update_matches_with_options
nodes.summary: Kicks off an async delegate match update for the current query, canceling any pending update and tracking scroll behavior for when results arrive.

nodes.name: matches_updated
nodes.summary: Handles completion of an async match update, adjusting selection and scroll position based on the new result set.

nodes.name: render_element
nodes.summary: Renders a single picker result row, including selection/multi-select indicators and delegate-provided content.

nodes.name: confirm
nodes.summary: Handles the confirm action on the currently selected picker item, delegating to the PickerDelegate's confirm logic.

nodes.name: set_preview_layout
nodes.summary: Updates the picker's preview pane layout (right/below/hidden), persisting the new preference.

nodes.name: popover_menu.rs
nodes.summary: Wraps a Picker in a popover-menu-style trigger component (PickerPopoverMenu) for use as a dropdown-triggered search/selection widget.

nodes.name: PickerPopoverMenu
nodes.summary: Component combining a trigger element with a Picker shown in a popover, supporting anchor/offset/tooltip configuration.

nodes.name: preview.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Preview pane abstraction and PreviewBackend trait for showing file/buffer/symbol content alongside picker results.

nodes.name: Preview
nodes.summary: Holds the current preview content and layout, delegating rendering/update/clear operations to a PreviewBackend implementation.

nodes.name: PreviewBackend
nodes.summary: Trait implemented by picker-specific preview renderers to update, render, resize, and clear preview content.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Describes a preview content update, constructible from a file path, buffer, symbol, or plain message, plus an optional match location.

nodes.name: render.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Picker's top-level Render trait, laying out the head, results list, optional preview pane, and footer according to the current shape and preview layout.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Top-level render implementation for Picker, dispatching to preview-below, preview-right, or no-preview layout renderers based on current state.

nodes.name: render_results
nodes.summary: Renders the scrollable results list/uniform-list area of the picker, including empty-state and scrollbar handling.

nodes.name: render_with_preview_right
nodes.summary: Renders the picker with its preview pane positioned to the right of the results list, including a resizable divider.

nodes.name: finish_any_completed_resize
nodes.summary: Finalizes an in-progress picker resize drag once complete, persisting the new shape.

nodes.name: shape.rs
nodes.summary: Geometry and layout math for picker windows: computes clamped positions/sizes for the results and preview panes across resizing, centering, and viewport-fraction modes.

nodes.name: Shape
nodes.summary: Represents the current resizing/positioning state of a picker window, exposing methods to compute pane positions, clamp sizes, and persist width/height changes.

nodes.name: SizeBounds
nodes.summary: Defines minimum/maximum size constraints for the picker and its panes, with clamp helper methods for width, height, and divider position.

nodes.name: ViewportFraction
nodes.summary: Represents a size as a fraction of the viewport, convertible to/from absolute pixel values given the current window bounds.

nodes.name: picker_position_and_size
nodes.summary: Computes the overall clamped position and size of the picker window for the given layout and window bounds.

nodes.name: results_position_and_size
nodes.summary: Computes the position and size of the results pane within the overall picker bounds for the given layout.

nodes.name: preview_position_and_size
nodes.summary: Computes the position and size of the preview pane within the overall picker bounds for the given layout.

nodes.name: clamp_position_and_size
nodes.summary: Clamps a working position/size against min/max bounds and viewport edges for the given layout and window.

nodes.name: apply_results_size
nodes.summary: Applies computed size constraints to the results pane's div element during rendering.

nodes.name: bindable.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Bind and Column traits used to convert Rust values to and from SQLite statement bindings, with implementations for primitive types, strings, blobs, paths, UUIDs, and Option/tuple wrappers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses repeated trait impl blocks (Bind/Column/StaticColumnCount) for many primitive and composite types rather than macros, resulting in a long but mechanically repetitive file.

nodes.name: StaticColumnCount
nodes.summary: Trait reporting how many SQL columns a Rust type occupies when bound or read, used to compute offsets for composite bindings.

nodes.name: Bind
nodes.summary: Trait for binding a Rust value into a prepared SQLite Statement at a given parameter index.

nodes.name: Column
nodes.summary: Trait for reading a Rust value back out of a SQLite Statement's result column at a given index.

nodes.name: connection.rs
nodes.summary: Wraps a raw libsqlite3-sys connection handle, providing safe open/backup/error-handling APIs and a write-lock guard, plus a syntax-checking helper used before applying ALTER TABLE migrations.

nodes.name: Connection
nodes.summary: RAII wrapper around a raw sqlite3 pointer with helpers for opening file/memory databases, backups, error retrieval, and serialized write access.

nodes.name: open_with_flags
nodes.summary: Opens a SQLite connection at the given URI with explicit sqlite3_open_v2 flags and enables extended result codes.

nodes.name: open_memory
nodes.summary: Opens an in-memory SQLite database, using a named shared memory URI when persistence-like sharing across connections is requested.

nodes.name: backup_main
nodes.summary: Performs a full sqlite3_backup of the main database into another Connection using the SQLite online backup API.

nodes.name: sql_has_syntax_error
nodes.summary: Validates SQL syntax by preparing statements against a scratch in-memory database, special-casing ALTER TABLE statements by pre-creating a placeholder table/column so the syntax check succeeds independent of schema state.

nodes.name: last_error
nodes.summary: Retrieves the last SQLite error code and message from the connection, returning Ok when the code is a known non-error code.

nodes.name: parse_alter_table
nodes.summary: Hand-parses an ALTER TABLE statement's remaining SQL to extract the target table name and, for RENAME/DROP COLUMN forms, the referenced column name.

nodes.name: domain.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Domain trait that scopes migrations to a named area of the database and a Migrator trait for applying domain migrations to a Connection.

nodes.name: Domain
nodes.summary: Trait identifying a named migration domain and controlling whether a given migration change is allowed to proceed.

nodes.name: Migrator
nodes.summary: Trait for types that can run their associated domain's migrations against a Connection.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for sqlez that declares and re-exports the bindable, connection, domain, migrations, savepoint, statement, thread_safe_connection, typed_statements, and util modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust crate root (lib.rs) acting as a module barrel, analogous to an index.ts entry point.

nodes.name: migrations.rs
nodes.summary: Implements schema migration execution for a domain, tracking applied migrations in a migrations table, running each pending migration inside its own transaction, and cleaning up rows with orphaned foreign keys.

nodes.name: eager_exec
nodes.summary: Executes SQL immediately (rather than lazily), splitting the statement string for eager evaluation semantics used during migration application.

nodes.name: migrate
nodes.summary: Core migration runner: creates the migrations tracking table if absent, determines which migrations have already run, and applies remaining migrations for a domain in order inside transactions.

nodes.name: delete_rows_with_orphaned_foreign_key_references
nodes.summary: Scans the database schema for foreign key constraints and deletes rows whose referenced parent rows no longer exist, used as a migration cleanup pass.

nodes.name: savepoint.rs
nodes.summary: Provides SAVEPOINT-based nested transaction helpers that run a closure within a named savepoint and either release or roll it back based on the closure's result.

nodes.name: with_savepoint
nodes.summary: Runs a closure inside a named SQLite SAVEPOINT, releasing the savepoint on success and rolling back on failure.

nodes.name: with_savepoint_rollback
nodes.summary: Runs a closure inside a named SAVEPOINT and always rolls back afterward regardless of outcome, useful for dry-run style operations.

nodes.name: statement.rs
nodes.summary: Wraps a prepared SQLite statement (sqlite3_stmt), exposing bind_* and column_* primitives plus higher-level step/map/single/maybe iteration helpers built on the Bind/Column traits.

nodes.name: Statement
nodes.summary: RAII wrapper around a raw sqlite3_stmt pointer tied to a borrowed Connection, exposing binding and column-reading primitives.

nodes.name: StepResult
nodes.summary: Enum representing the outcome of stepping a prepared statement (row available, done, or misuse).

nodes.name: SqlType
nodes.summary: Enum mirroring SQLite's dynamic column type tags (Text, Integer, Blob, Real, Null).

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Prepares a SQL query string into a Statement against a given Connection, translating SQLite prepare errors into contextual Results.

nodes.name: bind_index_with
nodes.summary: Internal helper that binds a value at a specific parameter index using a provided low-level bind callback, checking the SQLite result code.

nodes.name: column_blob
nodes.summary: Reads a BLOB column's raw bytes from the current result row as a byte slice.

nodes.name: column_text
nodes.summary: Reads a TEXT column's value from the current result row as a UTF-8 string slice.

nodes.name: column_type
nodes.summary: Determines the dynamic SqlType of a result column at the given index using sqlite3_column_type.

nodes.name: step
nodes.summary: Advances the prepared statement to the next result row, translating sqlite3_step's raw code into a StepResult or error.

nodes.name: map
nodes.summary: Iterates all result rows of the statement, applying a callback to each row's columns and collecting the mapped results into a Vec.

nodes.name: single
nodes.summary: Executes the statement expecting exactly one result row, erroring if zero or more than one row is returned.

nodes.name: maybe
nodes.summary: Executes the statement expecting zero or one result rows, returning an Option instead of erroring when no row is found.

nodes.name: thread_safe_connection.rs
nodes.summary: Provides a thread-safe wrapper around Connection that serializes writes through a background queue thread while allowing concurrent reads, via ThreadSafeConnection and its builder.

nodes.name: ThreadSafeConnection
nodes.summary: Shared, cloneable handle to a SQLite connection that queues write operations onto a dedicated background thread for serialized access.

nodes.name: ThreadSafeConnectionBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder for configuring and constructing a ThreadSafeConnection with a custom initialization query and write queue.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Finalizes the builder, opening the underlying Connection, running the initialize query, and spawning the background write-queue thread.

nodes.name: initialize_queues
nodes.summary: Sets up the shared write-queue state map used to coordinate write access across ThreadSafeConnection instances sharing the same database.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Creates a ThreadSafeConnectionBuilder for the given URI and persistence flag.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Submits a write callback to the background queue thread and blocks until it completes, providing exclusive write access to the connection.

nodes.name: create_connection
nodes.summary: Opens and initializes a new underlying Connection instance for use by the write-queue thread, running the configured initialization query.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a new ThreadSafeConnection from a URI, persistence flag, initialization query, and write queue constructor.

nodes.name: background_thread_queue
nodes.summary: Spawns and returns a background OS thread that owns a Connection and processes queued write callbacks sequentially.

nodes.name: typed_statements.rs
nodes.summary: Extends Connection with typed helpers (exec, exec_bound, select, select_row, select_row_bound) that compile SQL into Statements and map results using the Bind/Column traits.

nodes.name: select_row_bound
nodes.summary: Returns a closure that binds input parameters, executes a query, and returns at most one typed result row.

nodes.name: util.rs
nodes.summary: Small utility module providing UnboundedSyncSender, a Sync-safe wrapper enabling an unbounded channel sender to be shared across the write-queue's threads.

nodes.name: UnboundedSyncSender
nodes.summary: Wraps an unbounded channel Sender to mark it as Sync so it can be captured by closures shared across threads.

nodes.name: anchor.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Anchor type, a version-independent position within a CRDT buffer expressed as a Lamport timestamp plus insertion offset and bias, so positions survive concurrent edits. Provides comparison, clamping (bias), and validity helpers plus range extension traits.
nodes.languageNotes: Anchor positions encode timestamp+offset+bias so they can be resolved against any buffer version, the key to stable references across collaborative edits.

nodes.name: Anchor
nodes.summary: A stable, version-independent position in a buffer keyed by a Lamport timestamp, insertion offset, and bias; the min/max helpers and cmp let anchors be ordered and clamped relative to a given buffer.

nodes.name: AnchorRangeExt
nodes.summary: Extension trait adding cmp, overlaps, and contains_anchor operations to ranges of anchors, resolved against a buffer.

nodes.name: locator.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Locator, a dense fractional identifier (SmallVec of u64) used to order buffer fragments in the sum-tree; the between() method mints a new locator strictly between two neighbors so fragments can be inserted without renumbering.
nodes.languageNotes: Fractional indexing: locators form a dense total order so a new element can always be placed between any two existing ones, avoiding global reindexing on insert.

nodes.name: Locator
nodes.summary: A dense fractional index (backed by a SmallVec of u64 digits) giving fragments a stable total order; between() generates an identifier lying strictly between two existing locators.

nodes.name: network.rs
nodes.summary: Test-support simulation of a peer network for the CRDT: routes operation Envelopes between per-peer inboxes, supports disconnect/reconnect and randomized broadcast to exercise concurrent-edit convergence.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated behind test/test-support; models message delivery so property tests can assert CRDT convergence under arbitrary interleavings.

nodes.name: Network
nodes.summary: In-memory peer network holding per-peer inboxes and a disconnected set; broadcast randomly orders delivery and receive drains a peer's ready messages to simulate concurrent replication.

nodes.name: operation_queue.rs
nodes.summary: A sum-tree-backed priority queue of pending CRDT operations keyed by Lamport timestamp, used to hold deferred operations until their causal dependencies arrive. Supports insert, drain, and iteration in timestamp order.

nodes.name: OperationQueue
nodes.summary: SumTree-based queue ordering pending operations by their Lamport timestamp key, exposing insert/drain/iter so deferred ops can be replayed once dependencies are satisfied.

nodes.name: OperationSummary
nodes.summary: Sum-tree summary aggregating the max key and total length of queued operations so the queue can be searched and sized in logarithmic time.

nodes.name: patch.rs
nodes.summary: Defines Patch, an ordered set of non-overlapping Edits describing how one text version maps to another. The heart is compose(), which merges a second patch into this one to produce a single old-to-new transformation, plus inversion and old/new position mapping.
nodes.languageNotes: compose() is the central diff-algebra operation: composing two consecutive patches into one preserves the old->new mapping across chained edits.

nodes.name: Patch
nodes.summary: An ordered, non-overlapping list of Edits representing a transformation between two buffer versions; supports composition of consecutive patches, inversion, and mapping positions between old and new coordinate spaces.

nodes.name: compose
nodes.summary: Merges a following iterator of edits into this patch, producing a single patch that maps the original text directly to the final text by interleaving and coalescing overlapping edit ranges.

nodes.name: edit_for_old_position
nodes.summary: Finds the edit (if any) that affects a given position in the old coordinate space, used when translating positions through the patch.

nodes.name: old_to_new
nodes.summary: Maps a position in the old text to its corresponding position in the new text by accumulating the length deltas of preceding edits.

nodes.name: selection.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the generic Selection type (head/tail anchors, reversed flag, and a SelectionGoal for vertical-movement column memory) plus operations to move, collapse, and resolve selections against a snapshot.
nodes.languageNotes: SelectionGoal preserves the desired horizontal column across up/down movement even over short lines, a standard editor UX detail.

nodes.name: Selection
nodes.summary: A generic text selection with start/end positions, a reversed flag distinguishing head from tail, and a SelectionGoal; provides head/tail accessors, set_head/set_tail movement, and resolution to concrete offsets against a snapshot.

nodes.name: subscription.rs
nodes.summary: A lightweight publish/subscribe mechanism (Topic and Subscription) that delivers coalesced edit patches to interested consumers, letting downstream views react to buffer changes since their last poll.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Comprehensive unit and randomized property-test suite for the text buffer: exercises editing, anchors, undo/redo, transaction history, concurrent-edit convergence, line-ending handling, and large-insertion fragment splitting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses randomized concurrent-edit tests (test_random_concurrent_edits) driven by the network simulation to assert CRDT convergence across replicas.

nodes.name: test_random_edits
nodes.summary: Randomized property test applying arbitrary sequences of edits to a buffer and asserting text, anchors, and version bookkeeping stay consistent.

nodes.name: test_random_concurrent_edits
nodes.summary: Randomized test simulating multiple replicas editing concurrently through the network simulation and asserting all peers converge to identical buffer state.

nodes.name: test_anchors
nodes.summary: Verifies anchor creation, bias behavior, and that anchors resolve to correct positions across a series of edits.

nodes.name: test_history
nodes.summary: Exercises transaction grouping, undo/redo stacks, and history bookkeeping to confirm transactions can be grouped, finalized, and reverted correctly.

nodes.name: text.rs
nodes.summary: The core CRDT text buffer implementation and crate root. Buffer/BufferSnapshot store text as a sum-tree of Fragments identified by Locators and Lamport timestamps, enabling conflict-free concurrent editing, stable anchors, transactional undo/redo, deferred remote operations, and coordinate conversions across offset/point/UTF-16 spaces.
nodes.languageNotes: A fragment-based CRDT: text is a SumTree of Fragments ordered by Locator, each tagged with a Lamport timestamp and undo state, so concurrent edits from any replica merge deterministically. MAX_INSERTION_LEN splits large inserts so u32 relative offsets suffice.

nodes.name: Buffer
nodes.summary: The mutable CRDT text buffer: owns a BufferSnapshot, transaction History, a Lamport clock, deferred-operation queue, and edit subscriptions. Applies local and remote edits, resolves anchors, and drives undo/redo, exposing the primary editing API of the crate.

nodes.name: BufferSnapshot
nodes.summary: An immutable, cheaply-cloned view of buffer state (visible/deleted rope, fragment sum-tree, insertions, undo map, version). Provides all read-only queries: text extraction, anchor resolution, coordinate conversions, line metrics, and edit diffing since a prior version.

nodes.name: History
nodes.summary: Manages the buffer's transactional edit history: undo/redo stacks, transaction grouping within a time interval, and operations needed to start, end, group, and finalize transactions.

nodes.name: Fragment
nodes.summary: The atomic unit of the CRDT: a contiguous run of inserted text tagged with a Locator id, Lamport timestamp, length, visibility, and the set of deletions/undos affecting it; visibility depends on version and undo state.

nodes.name: LineEnding
nodes.summary: Enum of Unix vs Windows line endings with detection from text and normalization helpers that rewrite CRLF/CR to the buffer's canonical newline representation.

nodes.name: LineIndent
nodes.summary: Computes and represents a line's leading indentation as tab and space counts (and whether the line is blank), built from text chunks and convertible to a display length given a tab size.

nodes.name: Operation
nodes.summary: The CRDT operation enum (Edit or Undo) carrying replica id, Lamport timestamp, and causal version; the replicated unit exchanged between peers to reconstruct buffer state.

nodes.name: RopeBuilder
nodes.summary: Incrementally rebuilds the visible and deleted ropes while walking old fragment cursors during an edit, pushing text and length runs to produce the new buffer content efficiently.

nodes.name: undo_map.rs
nodes.summary: Implements UndoMap, a sum-tree tracking how many times each edit has been undone, so fragment visibility can be recomputed for any buffer version by consulting undo counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Storing undo counts per edit id (rather than mutating fragments) lets visibility be evaluated against any historical version, essential for CRDT undo in a collaborative setting.

nodes.name: UndoMap
nodes.summary: Sum-tree mapping edit ids to undo counts; is_undone/was_undone/undo_count answer whether an edit is currently or was historically undone at a given version, driving fragment visibility.

nodes.name: dispatcher.rs
nodes.summary: Implements GPUI's PlatformDispatcher for the WebAssembly target, routing tasks to the main thread via a mailbox and Web Worker message-posting loop since browsers have no native OS threads for arbitrary task execution.
nodes.languageNotes: Targets wasm32 and simulates multithreaded dispatch using postMessage-based signaling since Web Workers cannot block on channels the way native threads can.

nodes.name: MainThreadItem
nodes.summary: Represents a unit of work (a Runnable plus optional priority/window context) queued for execution on the browser's main thread.

nodes.name: MainThreadMailbox
nodes.summary: Queue that collects MainThreadItems posted from any thread and drains/signals them for execution on the browser main thread's event loop.

nodes.name: WebDispatcher
nodes.summary: GPUI PlatformDispatcher implementation for the web platform, scheduling immediate, delayed, and realtime tasks through the MainThreadMailbox.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Pops and executes all queued MainThreadItems for the given window on the calling (main) thread.

nodes.name: run_waker_loop
nodes.summary: Runs a self-rescheduling animation-frame based loop that repeatedly drains the mailbox, effectively acting as the main-thread task pump for the wasm target.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a WebDispatcher, optionally spawning a Web Worker thread pool when threading is allowed by the browser environment.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Schedules a background Runnable for execution, either on a worker thread or the main thread mailbox depending on availability.

nodes.name: dispatch_after
nodes.summary: Schedules a Runnable to run after a delay using a browser setTimeout-backed timer.

nodes.name: spawn_realtime
nodes.summary: Spawns a closure on a real OS/worker thread for latency-sensitive work when multithreading is available in the browser.

nodes.name: execute_on_main_thread
nodes.summary: Posts a MainThreadItem into the mailbox and signals the browser event loop to drain it on the main thread.

nodes.name: schedule_runnable
nodes.summary: Chooses whether to run a Runnable immediately or via execute_on_main_thread based on priority and current thread context.

nodes.name: display.rs
nodes.summary: Implements GPUI's PlatformDisplay trait for the browser, reporting the (single, virtual) display's screen and viewport dimensions and default window bounds.

nodes.name: WebDisplay
nodes.summary: Represents the browser viewport as a GPUI PlatformDisplay, exposing screen size, id, and default window bounds derived from the DOM window.

nodes.name: screen_size
nodes.summary: Reads the browser window.screen dimensions and converts them into a GPUI Size in pixels.

nodes.name: viewport_size
nodes.summary: Reads the browser window's inner viewport dimensions and converts them into a GPUI Size in pixels.

nodes.name: default_bounds
nodes.summary: Computes default window bounds centered within the viewport for newly created windows.

nodes.name: events.rs
nodes.summary: Registers and translates browser DOM events (pointer, wheel, keyboard, drag-and-drop, focus, composition) into GPUI's platform-agnostic input event types for the web window.

nodes.name: WebEventListeners
nodes.summary: Holds the collection of registered DOM event listener closures for a web window so they can be kept alive and later dropped.

nodes.name: ClickState
nodes.summary: Tracks recent click position and timing to detect multi-click (double/triple click) sequences for pointer events.

nodes.name: register_click
nodes.summary: Updates ClickState with a new click's position/time and determines the resulting click count for multi-click detection.

nodes.name: register_event_listeners
nodes.summary: Registers the full set of DOM event listeners (pointer, wheel, keyboard, drag, paste, focus, composition) on the window's canvas element.

nodes.name: listen
nodes.summary: Generic helper that attaches a DOM event listener closure to an element and stores the closure to keep it alive.

nodes.name: listen_input
nodes.summary: Attaches a listener to a hidden input/textarea element used for capturing IME and composition text input.

nodes.name: listen_non_passive
nodes.summary: Attaches a non-passive DOM event listener (allowing preventDefault) for events like wheel and touch that need to block default browser behavior.

nodes.name: register_pointer_down
nodes.summary: Registers the pointerdown DOM listener, converting it into a GPUI MouseDownEvent including click-count and button detection.

nodes.name: register_pointer_up
nodes.summary: Registers the pointerup DOM listener, converting it into a GPUI MouseUpEvent.

nodes.name: register_pointer_move
nodes.summary: Registers the pointermove DOM listener, converting it into a GPUI MouseMoveEvent with current pressed-button state.

nodes.name: register_pointer_leave
nodes.summary: Registers the pointerleave DOM listener, notifying GPUI that the pointer left the window bounds.

nodes.name: register_wheel
nodes.summary: Registers a non-passive wheel event listener, converting browser scroll deltas into GPUI ScrollWheelEvents.

nodes.name: register_dragover
nodes.summary: Registers the dragover DOM listener to track drag-and-drop position over the window during file drag operations.

nodes.name: register_drop
nodes.summary: Registers the drop DOM listener, extracting dropped file paths and dispatching a GPUI file-drop event.

nodes.name: register_key_down
nodes.summary: Registers the keydown DOM listener, translating browser KeyboardEvent codes/modifiers into GPUI KeyDownEvent with proper key-char resolution.

nodes.name: register_key_up
nodes.summary: Registers the keyup DOM listener, translating browser KeyboardEvents into GPUI KeyUpEvent.

nodes.name: register_paste
nodes.summary: Registers the paste DOM listener to capture clipboard text and forward it into GPUI's input handling.

nodes.name: register_composition_update
nodes.summary: Registers the compositionupdate DOM listener for IME text composition previews.

nodes.name: register_composition_end
nodes.summary: Registers the compositionend DOM listener to finalize IME-composed text input.

nodes.name: register_focus
nodes.summary: Registers the focus DOM listener, notifying GPUI that the window gained input focus.

nodes.name: register_blur
nodes.summary: Registers the blur DOM listener, notifying GPUI that the window lost input focus.

nodes.name: register_pointer_enter
nodes.summary: Registers the pointerenter DOM listener to notify GPUI the pointer entered the window bounds.

nodes.name: register_pointer_leave_hover
nodes.summary: Registers an additional pointerleave listener specifically to clear hover state in GPUI.

nodes.name: dom_key_to_gpui_key
nodes.summary: Maps a browser KeyboardEvent's code/key into GPUI's internal key-name representation, including special-case handling for shifted number keys.

nodes.name: is_mac_platform
nodes.summary: Detects whether the browser is running on macOS via navigator.platform/userAgent sniffing, used to select correct modifier key semantics.

nodes.name: compute_key_char
nodes.summary: Determines the printable character produced by a key event given current modifier state, accounting for shift/altgr combinations.

nodes.name: extract_file_paths_from_drag
nodes.summary: Extracts file names/paths from a DataTransfer object during a drag-and-drop event.

nodes.name: gpui_web.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for gpui_web that declares and re-exports the dispatcher, display, events, http_client, keyboard, logging, platform, and window modules implementing GPUI's WebAssembly backend.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust crate root acting as a module barrel for the wasm32 GPUI platform backend.

nodes.name: http_client.rs

nodes.name: adapt_to_json_schema_subset

nodes.name: collapse_nullable_only_any_of

nodes.name: parse_csv_with_positions

nodes.summary: Builds a TableLikeContent from a buffer snapshot: parses cells with positions, normalizes column count, splits header from body rows, and maps cells to buffer-anchored TableCells.

nodes.name: CsvPreviewSettings

nodes.name: TableDataEngine
nodes.summary: Holds the parsed table contents, the active filter stack, available filters, applied sorting, and the current display-to-data mapping for the preview.

nodes.name: DisplayToDataMapping

nodes.name: merge_mappings
nodes.summary: Merges the sorted order and retained (filtered) row set into an Arc-shared DisplayRow-to-DataRow index map.

nodes.name: rope.rs
nodes.summary: Core rope data structure for the editor's text buffer, storing UTF-8 text as a SumTree (B+-tree) of fixed-size chunks so that edits, slicing, and coordinate conversions run in logarithmic time. Exposes the full navigation and dimension-conversion API (offset/point/UTF-16) plus cursor, chunk, byte, and line iterators that every higher text layer builds on.
nodes.languageNotes: Built on sum_tree::SumTree with pluggable Dimension/TextDimension summaries; uses rayon for parallel chunk construction (from_str) and heapless ArrayVec for stack-allocated chunk batching.

nodes.name: chunk.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the fixed-capacity Chunk (a leaf of the rope's SumTree) and its zero-copy ChunkSlice view, encoding char boundaries, UTF-16 char positions, newlines, and tabs as parallel bitmaps so per-chunk offset/point conversions reduce to bit-twiddling (masks, popcount, leading/trailing zeros).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Bitmap type (u128-scale) with unbounded_shl/shr and count_ones for branchless position math; ArrayString for inline fixed-capacity text storage; includes nth_set_bit helpers implementing a parallel-bit select over 64-bit words.

nodes.name: point.rs
nodes.summary: Defines Point, a (row, column) coordinate in UTF-8 byte columns used throughout the rope for line/column addressing, with arithmetic, ordering, saturating subtraction, and str parsing helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements Add/Sub/AddAssign/Ord operator traits so points compose like scalars while respecting row-carry semantics on column overflow.

nodes.name: point_utf16.rs
nodes.summary: Defines PointUtf16, a (row, column) coordinate measured in UTF-16 code units, the coordinate system LSP and many external protocols expect, with the same arithmetic and ordering trait suite as Point.

nodes.name: offset_utf16.rs
nodes.summary: Defines OffsetUtf16, a newtype wrapping an absolute offset counted in UTF-16 code units, with Add/Sub/AddAssign operators so it participates in the rope's dimension arithmetic.

nodes.name: unclipped.rs
nodes.summary: Defines Unclipped<T>, a wrapper marking a coordinate that may fall outside valid text bounds or on a non-char-boundary, forcing callers to clip it explicitly before use so out-of-range positions cannot silently propagate.
nodes.languageNotes: A newtype-as-marker pattern: the type system distinguishes clipped from unclipped positions, turning a runtime invariant into a compile-time obligation.

nodes.name: Rope
nodes.summary: The rope text buffer: a SumTree of Chunk leaves. Provides append/replace/slice/push mutation, all offset/point/UTF-16 coordinate conversions, char/byte/chunk/line iterators, and clipping — the primary text abstraction consumed by the text and editor crates.

nodes.name: TextSummary
nodes.summary: Aggregate summary stored at each SumTree node (byte len, UTF-16 len, line/point extents, longest row, first/last line metrics), enabling O(log n) coordinate lookups by combining child summaries during tree traversal.

nodes.name: TextDimension
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting any measurable dimension of text (offset, Point, PointUtf16, OffsetUtf16) so the rope's seek/conversion machinery is generic over the coordinate system being queried.

nodes.name: Cursor
nodes.summary: Stateful forward cursor over the rope that seeks and slices by offset, accumulating a summary as it advances — the building block for range extraction and dimension conversion.

nodes.name: Chunks
nodes.summary: Bidirectional iterator over the rope's chunks within a range, supporting seek, line navigation (next_line/prev_line), and bitmap-aware peeking used by higher-level char, byte, and line iterators.

nodes.name: Bytes
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding raw bytes over a rope range (forward or reversed), implementing io::Read so rope regions can be streamed into byte-oriented consumers.

nodes.name: Lines
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding successive lines of the rope, seeking by offset and tracking position — used by editors and diagnostics to walk buffer content line by line.

nodes.name: Chunk
nodes.summary: A fixed-capacity leaf of the rope holding inline text plus precomputed bitmaps for char boundaries, UTF-16 chars, newlines, and tabs, enabling branchless per-chunk offset/point conversions and text summarization.

nodes.name: ChunkSlice
nodes.summary: A zero-copy borrowed view into a Chunk's text and bitmaps, exposing the full conversion/clipping API (split_at, slice, offset_to_point, clip_point, point_utf16_to_offset, etc.) without owning or copying data.

nodes.name: Tabs
nodes.summary: Iterator over tab positions within a chunk, returning each tab's byte and char offset by walking the tabs bitmap via trailing-zero scans.

nodes.name: Point
nodes.summary: A (row, column) position in UTF-8 byte columns with arithmetic, ordering, saturating subtraction, and parse_str construction from text.

nodes.name: PointUtf16
nodes.summary: A (row, column) position measured in UTF-16 code units with the full arithmetic and ordering trait suite, matching the coordinate system used by LSP and other external protocols.

nodes.name: OffsetUtf16
nodes.summary: Newtype for an absolute offset in UTF-16 code units, implementing Add/Sub/AddAssign so it composes in the rope's generic dimension arithmetic.

nodes.name: Unclipped
nodes.summary: Generic marker wrapper for a possibly-out-of-bounds coordinate; implements the SumTree dimension traits so unclipped positions flow through summaries but must be explicitly clipped before indexing.

nodes.name: push
nodes.summary: Appends text to the rope, splitting it across chunk-capacity boundaries at valid char boundaries and pushing completed chunks into the SumTree while coalescing small tails.

nodes.name: push_large
nodes.summary: Fast path for appending large text by chunking it in parallel (rayon) and bulk-inserting the resulting leaves into the SumTree.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Replaces a byte range of the rope with new text by slicing around the range and reassembling the pieces.

nodes.name: point_utf16_to_offset_impl
nodes.summary: Core conversion from a UTF-16 (row, column) point to an absolute byte offset, seeking the SumTree to the row then delegating to the target chunk's bitmap math, with optional clipping.

nodes.name: clip_point
nodes.summary: Clamps a Point to a valid position within the rope, snapping to a char/grapheme boundary in the requested bias direction by seeking to the row and deferring to the chunk clipper.

nodes.name: starts_with
nodes.summary: Tests whether the rope begins with a given string pattern by streaming chunks and comparing without materializing the full text.

nodes.name: ends_with
nodes.summary: Tests whether the rope ends with a given string pattern by streaming chunks in reverse and comparing without materializing the full text.

nodes.name: next_line
nodes.summary: Advances the Chunks iterator to the start of the next line using newline bitmaps to jump chunk-to-chunk without scanning every byte.

nodes.name: prev_line
nodes.summary: Moves the Chunks iterator backward to the start of the previous line via reverse newline-bitmap scans, mirroring next_line for upward navigation.

nodes.name: equals_str
nodes.summary: Compares the current chunk-iteration region against a string slice byte-for-byte across chunk boundaries, used to match patterns without allocation.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: io::Read implementation for the Bytes iterator, copying rope bytes into a caller buffer across chunk boundaries so rope ranges can be streamed.

nodes.name: add_assign
nodes.summary: Combines one TextSummary into another (the SumTree monoid operation), correctly merging line counts, longest-row tracking, and first/last-line metrics across a concatenation boundary.

nodes.name: from
nodes.summary: Constructs a TextSummary from a text slice, scanning it once to compute byte/UTF-16 lengths, line extents, and longest-row statistics for a new chunk.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Builds a Chunk from a text slice, scanning bytes to populate the char-boundary, UTF-16-char, newline, and tab bitmaps that back all later constant-time conversions.

nodes.name: prepend
nodes.summary: Prepends another chunk slice to this chunk, rebuilding text and shifting the bitmaps to keep boundary metadata consistent.

nodes.name: split_at
nodes.summary: Splits a ChunkSlice at a byte offset into two slices, partitioning each bitmap with shift-and-mask so both halves retain correct char/newline/tab metadata.

nodes.name: slice
nodes.summary: Extracts a sub-slice of a ChunkSlice for a byte range, asserting char boundaries and masking each bitmap down to the requested window.

nodes.name: text_summary
nodes.summary: Produces the aggregate TextSummary for a chunk slice (length, UTF-16 length, line count, longest row, first/last line metrics) by combining bitmap popcounts.

nodes.name: longest_row
nodes.summary: Computes the longest row (in chars) within a chunk and its char count by walking the newline bitmap and counting chars between consecutive newlines with popcount.

nodes.name: point_to_offset
nodes.summary: Converts a (row, column) Point to a byte offset within a chunk by locating the row via the newline bitmap and adding the clamped column.

nodes.name: offset_utf16_to_offset
nodes.summary: Converts a UTF-16 code-unit offset to a byte offset within a chunk using nth_set_bit over the UTF-16 char bitmap to find the target boundary.

nodes.name: point_utf16_to_offset
nodes.summary: Converts a UTF-16 (row, column) point to a byte offset within a chunk, resolving the row then walking the row's slice to the UTF-16 column, with optional clipping to char boundaries.

nodes.name: unclipped_point_utf16_to_point
nodes.summary: Maps a possibly-out-of-bounds UTF-16 point to a clamped UTF-8 Point within a chunk, clipping row and column to valid boundaries.

nodes.name: clip_point
nodes.summary: Clips a Point to a valid grapheme boundary within a chunk using a GraphemeCursor and the requested bias, so cursor positions never land inside a multi-byte grapheme.

nodes.name: clip_offset_utf16
nodes.summary: Clamps a UTF-16 offset to a valid char boundary within a chunk, biasing left or right when the target lands mid-character.

nodes.name: offset_range_for_row
nodes.summary: Returns the byte range spanning a given row within a chunk by locating the surrounding newlines via nth_set_bit and trailing-zero scans over the newline bitmap.

nodes.name: nth_set_bit_u64
nodes.summary: Branchless parallel-bit selection returning the index of the n-th set bit in a 64-bit word, the primitive underpinning fast UTF-16-to-byte and row lookups.

nodes.name: floor_char_boundary
nodes.summary: Rounds a byte index down to the nearest UTF-8 char boundary within the chunk, guarding all offset-based slicing against splitting a multi-byte code point.

nodes.name: panic_char_boundary
nodes.summary: Builds and raises a detailed panic when an offset is asserted to be a char boundary but is not, reporting the offending character and surrounding context for debugging.

nodes.name: parse_str
nodes.summary: Computes the end Point of a string by counting its newlines and the length of the final line, used to measure inserted text.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds two Points with row-carry semantics: when the right operand spans rows, its column replaces rather than accumulates onto the left column.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Adds two PointUtf16 values with the same row-carry semantics as Point, in UTF-16 column units.

nodes.name: paths.rs

nodes.name: strings.rs

nodes.name: CharBag
nodes.summary: Bitset type storing which lowercase letters (and a few flags) appear in a string, enabling O(1) superset checks used to quickly reject non-matching fuzzy candidates.

nodes.name: Matcher
nodes.summary: Holds per-query fuzzy matching state (query characters, char bag, score/position matrices) and drives the recursive scoring algorithm for candidate strings and paths.

nodes.name: MatchCandidate
nodes.summary: Trait implemented by matchable candidate types (paths, strings) exposing their character bag and characters for use by the Matcher.

nodes.name: match_candidates

nodes.name: recursive_score_match
nodes.summary: Core recursive dynamic-programming routine that computes the best possible fuzzy-match score for aligning a query against a candidate path, memoizing partial results in the Matcher's score matrix.

nodes.name: PathMatchCandidate

nodes.name: match_path_sets
nodes.summary: Fuzzy matches a query against multiple PathMatchCandidateSet sources in parallel using the provided executor, merging and ranking results across all sets while respecting a cancel flag.

nodes.name: StringMatchCandidate
nodes.summary: Represents a candidate string (with id and precomputed char bag) eligible for fuzzy string matching, such as a command palette action.

nodes.name: StringMatch
nodes.summary: Represents a scored fuzzy match result for a string candidate, including matched character positions and UTF-16 range mapping helpers, with ordering for ranking.

nodes.name: match_strings
nodes.summary: Fuzzy matches a query against a list of string candidates in parallel using the provided executor, returning ranked StringMatch results up to max_results.

nodes.name: CodeHandler
nodes.summary: HandleTag implementation that renders inline code spans and fenced code blocks, and passes code text through verbatim via handle_text.

nodes.name: markdown_writer.rs

nodes.summary: Declares the concrete set of known feature flags used across the editor (Notebook, Panic, AcpBeta, DiffReview, tool flags, project panel undo/redo, agent worktree label, auto-watch), each implementing the FeatureFlag trait.

nodes.name: settings.rs
nodes.summary: Defines FeatureFlagsSettings for user-configurable flag overrides and generates a JSON schema describing all known flags for settings validation/autocomplete.

nodes.name: generate_feature_flags_schema
nodes.summary: Builds a JSON schema object describing all registered feature flags and their possible override values, for use in settings.json validation.

nodes.name: store.rs
nodes.summary: Implements FeatureFlagStore, the global GPUI state holding staff status and server-reported flags, resolving effective flag values by combining server data, settings overrides, and staff-only defaults.

nodes.name: FeatureFlagStore
nodes.summary: Global GPUI store tracking staff status, server flag payloads, and settings overrides; resolves the final variant key for any registered flag descriptor.

nodes.name: try_flag_value
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective value of a typed feature flag by checking global enablement, settings overrides, staff status, and server-provided flags in priority order.

nodes.name: resolved_key
nodes.summary: Resolves which variant key applies for a flag descriptor by evaluating precedence between global-enabled, user overrides, staff-only enablement, and server flags.

nodes.name: fuzzy_nucleo.rs
nodes.summary: Crate entry point for the nucleo-backed fuzzy matcher, defining the Query type, case-sensitivity/length-penalty options, and helper routines (case mismatch counting, score penalties, position mapping) shared by string and path matching.

nodes.name: Query
nodes.summary: Represents a compiled fuzzy search query, holding the nucleo Pattern, query characters, and char-bag prefilter used to quickly reject non-matching candidates.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Constructs a Query from a raw search string, applying smart-case detection and building the nucleo Pattern and char bag for prefiltering.

nodes.name: count_case_mismatches
nodes.summary: Counts how many matched characters differ in case from the query, used to compute a smart-case scoring penalty.

nodes.name: positions_from_sorted
nodes.summary: Converts sorted UTF-32 character indices from the matcher into UTF-8 byte positions within the original string.

nodes.name: matcher.rs
nodes.summary: Maintains a thread-safe pool of reusable nucleo Matcher instances (checked out and returned) to avoid reallocation overhead during parallel fuzzy matching.

nodes.name: get_matchers
nodes.summary: Retrieves N matcher instances from the shared pool, creating new ones as needed, each configured with the given match config.

nodes.name: paths.rs
nodes.summary: Implements fuzzy path matching over one or more candidate sets, scoring paths with a filename-match bonus and worktree distance tiebreaker, and parallelizing the search across CPU segments.

nodes.name: PathMatch
nodes.summary: A single scored path match result with its match positions, worktree id, and distance to a relative ancestor for ranking tiebreaks.

nodes.name: PathMatchCandidateSet
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting a source of path candidates (e.g. per-worktree file lists) that can be searched by match_path_sets.

nodes.name: path_match_helper
nodes.summary: Core scoring loop that matches a query against a batch of path candidates, applying char-bag prefiltering, nucleo scoring, filename bonus, and case penalties, pushing results into the output vector.

nodes.name: match_path_sets
nodes.summary: Public entry point for fuzzy-matching paths across multiple candidate sets in parallel, splitting work across CPU segments and merging/truncating results to max_results.

nodes.name: match_fixed_path_set
nodes.summary: Matches a query against a single fixed list of path candidates synchronously, used for smaller/simpler search scenarios than the parallel match_path_sets.

nodes.name: strings.rs
nodes.summary: Implements fuzzy matching over plain string candidates (used e.g. for command palette and symbol search), with both a synchronous match_strings and a parallel async match_strings_async, plus extensive unit tests covering scoring, cancellation, and segment partitioning.

nodes.name: StringMatch
nodes.summary: A single scored string match result with candidate id, score, matched character positions, and the matched string.

nodes.name: StringMatchCandidate
nodes.summary: Input candidate for string fuzzy matching, precomputing a char bag for fast prefiltering before the nucleo scoring pass.

nodes.name: match_strings_async
nodes.summary: Parallel fuzzy string search entry point that splits candidates across CPU-sized segments, matches each segment with a pooled matcher, and merges/truncates the top results.

nodes.name: match_strings
nodes.summary: Synchronous single-threaded fuzzy string search over a candidate list, used when parallelism is unnecessary.

nodes.name: match_string_helper
nodes.summary: Core per-segment scoring loop shared by match_strings and match_strings_async, applying char-bag prefiltering, nucleo scoring, case penalty, and length penalty.

nodes.name: example_editor.rs
nodes.summary: Core of the gpui text-editing example: defines the Editor entity holding text/cursor/blink state with full IME (EntityInputHandler) support, and a custom EditorText Element that lays out, prepaints, and paints shaped text lines plus the blinking cursor. Serves as the reference implementation extension writers copy when building notebook's markdown/LaTeX editing surfaces.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements gpui's low-level Element lifecycle (request_layout / prepaint / paint) by hand and satisfies EntityInputHandler with careful UTF-8/UTF-16 offset conversion for platform IME interop.

nodes.name: Editor
nodes.summary: Stateful gpui entity backing a text field: owns the text value entity, cursor byte offset, cursor-visibility flag, a blink background task, and focus subscriptions. Exposes editing operations (left/right/home/end/backspace/delete/insert_newline) and implements the EntityInputHandler trait so the OS IME can query and mutate its contents.

nodes.name: EditorText
nodes.summary: Custom gpui Element that renders an Editor entity: shapes each text line, positions the cursor quad, registers an ElementInputHandler for IME, and paints lines and cursor during the paint phase.

nodes.name: over
nodes.summary: Constructs an Editor over an existing shared text value entity, wiring focus/blur handlers to start/stop cursor blinking and observing the value entity to clamp the cursor to a valid char boundary when the text changes externally.

nodes.name: spawn_blink_task
nodes.summary: Spawns a background task that toggles cursor visibility on a fixed interval to produce the blink animation, notifying the entity on each toggle and exiting when the entity is dropped.

nodes.name: backspace
nodes.summary: Deletes the grapheme before the cursor using grapheme-aware boundary detection, updates the shared value entity, moves the cursor, and resets the blink timer.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Deletes the grapheme after the cursor using next-boundary detection and updates the shared value entity, then resets the blink timer.

nodes.name: offset_from_utf16
nodes.summary: Converts a UTF-16 code-unit offset (as supplied by the platform IME) into a UTF-8 byte offset within the given content string.

nodes.name: offset_to_utf16
nodes.summary: Converts a UTF-8 byte offset into a UTF-16 code-unit offset for reporting selection and marked ranges back to the platform IME.

nodes.name: text_for_range
nodes.summary: EntityInputHandler method returning the substring of the editor's text for a UTF-16 range requested by the IME, along with the actual clamped range.

nodes.name: replace_text_in_range
nodes.summary: EntityInputHandler method that replaces a UTF-16 range (or the current cursor position) with new text from the IME, updating the shared value entity and repositioning the cursor.

nodes.name: request_layout
nodes.summary: Element layout phase that computes the editor's height from its line count and the window line height, requesting a full-width layout node from the window.

nodes.name: prepaint
nodes.summary: Element prepaint phase that shapes each text line via the text system (or a placeholder), computes the cursor's pixel bounds from its line and offset, and returns the shaped lines plus an optional cursor quad for painting.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Element paint phase that registers the ElementInputHandler for IME, paints each shaped line at its origin, and fills the cursor quad when present.

nodes.name: cursor_line_and_offset
nodes.summary: Maps a byte cursor offset within multi-line content to a (line index, within-line byte offset) pair used to position the cursor during prepaint.

nodes.name: standard_actions
nodes.summary: Returns a closure that attaches the common editing actions (Left/Right/Home/End/Backspace/Delete) to an interactive element, each dispatching into the shared Editor entity. Reused by both Input and TextArea to share keybinding wiring.

nodes.name: example_input.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Input render component for the gpui view example: a single-line text field that can be sourced either from a plain String or an existing Editor entity, styled with focus shadow, border, and an IBeam cursor. Demonstrates the reusable input-box pattern for notebook's form-style fields.

nodes.name: Input
nodes.summary: Builder-style render component wrapping a text Source (String or Editor) with optional width and color overrides; its render method materializes an Editor, wires standard editing actions, and draws a focus-aware bordered input box.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the input box: obtains or creates the backing Editor via window state, computes focus-driven border/shadow styling, applies standard editing actions, and embeds the cached EditorText element.

nodes.name: example_text_area.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the TextArea render component for the gpui view example: a multi-row text field sourced from a String or Editor, adding an Enter keybinding for newline insertion on top of the shared editing actions. The multi-line analog of Input, relevant to notebook's note/memo composition surfaces.

nodes.name: TextArea
nodes.summary: Builder-style multi-row render component wrapping a text Source with configurable row count and color; its render method wires standard editing actions plus an Enter-to-newline action and sizes the box by row count.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the text area: resolves the backing Editor, applies standard editing actions plus an Enter keybinding that inserts a newline, and lays out a fixed-width multi-row bordered box embedding the cached EditorText element.

nodes.name: view_example_main.rs
nodes.summary: Entry point and root view of the gpui view example, wiring together Input, TextArea, and a CursorReadout into a demo window. Registers editor keybindings, opens the window, and provides both native (main) and web (start) launch paths.

nodes.name: CursorReadout
nodes.summary: Small render component that reads an Editor entity's cursor offset and displays it as text beside the input, demonstrating how a shared Editor exposes its state to sibling views.

nodes.name: ViewExample
nodes.summary: Root view of the example that lays out sections of String-backed and Editor-backed Inputs and TextAreas, allocating backing editors via window state and arranging them in a scrollable column.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the demo layout: allocates String and Editor window-state entities, then composes sections of Inputs, TextAreas, and CursorReadouts to showcase both text-source modes.

nodes.name: run_example
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the gpui application: binds the editor keybindings (arrows, home/end, backspace, delete), opens a centered window hosting ViewExample, and registers the quit action.

nodes.name: async_body.rs
nodes.summary: Defines AsyncBody, a request/response body abstraction that can wrap empty content, in-memory bytes, an async reader, or serialized JSON, implementing AsyncRead and http-body Body for streaming.

nodes.name: AsyncBody
nodes.summary: Enum-backed body type used throughout the HTTP client for request/response payloads, with From impls for bytes, strings, Vec<u8>, and JSON.

nodes.name: poll_read
nodes.summary: Implements AsyncRead for AsyncBody by dispatching to the empty, in-memory cursor, or async reader variant.

nodes.name: github.rs
nodes.summary: Client helpers for querying the GitHub releases API — fetching the latest release matching filters, fetching a release by tag, and building asset download URLs by archive kind.

nodes.name: latest_github_release
nodes.summary: Fetches all releases for a GitHub repo and returns the newest one matching pre-release and asset-presence filters, stripping digest prefixes from asset metadata.

nodes.name: get_release_by_tag_name
nodes.summary: Fetches a specific GitHub release by its tag name via the GitHub REST API.

nodes.name: build_asset_url
nodes.summary: Builds a GitHub release asset download URL for a given repo, tag, and archive kind (tar.gz, tar.bz2, gz, zip).

nodes.name: github_download.rs
nodes.summary: Downloads and installs binaries/archives from GitHub releases with digest verification, staging directory management, and archive extraction (tar.gz, tar.bz2, gz, zip) before atomically finalizing into the destination path.

nodes.name: GithubBinaryMetadata
nodes.summary: Persisted metadata (version, digest) tracking which binary release is currently installed, read from and written to a sidecar JSON file.

nodes.name: download_server_binary
nodes.summary: Downloads a language server or agent archive from a URL, extracts it into a staging directory with digest verification, and atomically moves it to the destination path.

nodes.name: download_server_raw_binary
nodes.summary: Downloads a raw (non-archived) binary from a URL, hashes it while streaming to disk, verifies the digest, marks it executable, and finalizes it into the destination path.

nodes.name: extract_to_staging
nodes.summary: Streams a downloaded archive body to a temp file while hashing it, verifies the digest against the expected value, then extracts the archive into the staging path.

nodes.name: stream_response_archive
nodes.summary: Dispatches archive extraction to the appropriate decoder (tar.gz, tar.bz2, gz, zip) based on asset kind, streaming directly from an HTTP response body.

nodes.name: http_client.rs
nodes.summary: Core HTTP client crate defining the HttpClient trait, proxy-aware and URL-scoped client wrappers (HttpClientWithProxy, HttpClientWithUrl), a BlockedHttpClient guard, and a FakeHttpClient for tests, plus Zed API/Cloud/LLM URL builders.

nodes.name: HttpClient
nodes.summary: Core async trait implemented by all HTTP client backends, exposing send, get, post_json, user_agent, proxy, and as_fake methods.

nodes.name: HttpClientWithUrl
nodes.summary: Wraps an HttpClientWithProxy with a configurable base URL and helpers to build Zed API, Cloud, and LLM endpoint URLs.

nodes.name: FakeHttpClient
nodes.summary: Test double implementing HttpClient with a swappable handler closure, plus convenience constructors for canned 404/200 responses.

nodes.name: BlockedHttpClient
nodes.summary: An HttpClient implementation that unconditionally rejects all requests with a permission-denied error, used to enforce network-disabled contexts.

nodes.name: build_zed_cloud_url
nodes.summary: Builds a fully-qualified Zed Cloud API URL by joining the configured base URL with the given path.

nodes.name: build_zed_llm_url
nodes.summary: Builds a Zed LLM service URL with query parameters, joining the configured base URL with the given path.

nodes.name: read_proxy_from_env
nodes.summary: Reads and parses a proxy URL from standard environment variables (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, etc.).

nodes.name: action_completion_provider.rs
nodes.summary: Implements a fuzzy-matching completion provider that suggests registered GPUI action names while editing keybinding action fields in the keymap editor.

nodes.name: ActionCompletionProvider
nodes.summary: Completion provider struct holding the list of registered action names and their humanized display names, used to drive editor autocompletion.

nodes.name: completions
nodes.summary: Computes fuzzy-matched action name completions for the current buffer position, normalizing the query and building GPUI Completion items on a background executor.

nodes.name: keymap_editor.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the full keymap editor UI panel: a searchable, filterable table of keybindings with conflict detection, plus a modal editor for creating and editing individual keybindings and their action arguments.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large GPUI view module (4392 lines, 22 structs/enums, 138 functions) combining state management, list rendering, JSON-based action-argument editing, and keystroke conflict resolution.

nodes.name: KeymapEditor
nodes.summary: Top-level GPUI view for the keymap editor panel, owning the searchable/filterable keybinding table, its query state, and modal-open handling.

nodes.name: KeybindingEditorModal
nodes.summary: Modal dialog view for creating or editing a single keybinding, including keystroke capture, context expression editing, and JSON action-argument validation.

nodes.name: ConflictState
nodes.summary: Tracks which keybindings conflict with each other by context and keystroke, used to render conflict warnings in the keybinding table.

nodes.name: ProcessedBinding
nodes.summary: Normalized, display-ready representation of a keybinding row combining the raw binding, its action information, context string, and conflict/unbound status.

nodes.name: render (KeymapEditor)
nodes.summary: Renders the main keymap editor panel UI: search/filter controls, the virtualized keybinding table, and conflict indicators.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Validates and persists an edited keybinding (action, context, arguments) back to the user's keymap file, handling create/update/conflict cases.

nodes.name: process_bindings
nodes.summary: Transforms raw registered key bindings into ProcessedBinding rows, resolving humanized action names, context expressions, and conflict status for display.

nodes.name: on_keymap_changed
nodes.summary: Handles global keymap-change notifications by reloading and reprocessing bindings and refreshing the editor's filtered view.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Registers the keymap editor panel and its actions with the workspace on crate initialization.

nodes.name: keystroke_input.rs
nodes.summary: Reusable GPUI input widget that records live keystroke sequences (including modifier-only chords) for building keybindings, with recording state, timers, and close-keystroke detection.

nodes.name: KeystrokeInput
nodes.summary: GPUI view component that captures and displays a sequence of keystrokes typed by the user, supporting recording, clearing, and a configurable close/stop binding.

nodes.name: render (KeystrokeInput)
nodes.summary: Renders the keystroke input field, showing recorded keystrokes or a recording indicator and action buttons.

nodes.name: handle_keystroke
nodes.summary: Processes an incoming keystroke event during recording, appending it to the captured sequence or triggering stop-recording logic.

nodes.name: handle_possible_close_keystroke
nodes.summary: Detects whether an incoming keystroke matches the configured close/stop binding and terminates recording accordingly.

nodes.name: on_modifiers_changed
nodes.summary: Tracks modifier-key-only chord changes while recording, allowing pure-modifier keybindings to be captured.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel that re-exports the keystroke_input UI component for use by the keymap editor.

nodes.name: extension.rs
nodes.summary: Provides an extension-facing proxy that lets Zed extensions register and unregister custom language model providers with the global registry.

nodes.name: LanguageModelProviderRegistryProxy
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around the language model provider registry exposing register/unregister hooks for the extension host API.

nodes.name: init_proxy
nodes.summary: Installs the LanguageModelProviderRegistryProxy as the global extension host proxy for language model provider registration.

nodes.name: language_models.rs
nodes.summary: Crate entry point that registers all built-in and OpenAI-compatible language model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, etc.) with the global registry based on user settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Central wiring point that reconciles user settings changes with dynamic provider registration/deregistration for OpenAI-API-compatible custom providers.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Crate initialization function that registers all supported language model providers and subscribes to settings changes to keep the registry in sync.

nodes.name: register_language_model_providers
nodes.summary: Registers each built-in language model provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock, Ollama, DeepSeek, etc.) into the provider registry with credentials and client dependencies.

nodes.name: register_compatible_providers
nodes.summary: Diffs old and new sets of user-configured OpenAI-API-compatible providers and registers/unregisters them accordingly.

nodes.name: from_settings
nodes.summary: Builds the set of currently configured OpenAI-API-compatible providers from user settings.

nodes.name: provider.rs
nodes.summary: Utility module for resolving custom HTTP headers for OpenAI-compatible language model providers while rejecting reserved header names.

nodes.name: resolve_custom_headers
nodes.summary: Merges user-configured custom headers for a provider, filtering out any that collide with reserved header names used internally.

nodes.name: settings.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the AllLanguageModelSettings struct aggregating per-provider settings (API URLs, models, custom headers) parsed from the user's settings.json.

nodes.name: AllLanguageModelSettings
nodes.summary: Top-level settings struct aggregating configuration for every supported language model provider, deserialized from user settings content.

nodes.name: from_settings
nodes.summary: Parses raw settings JSON content into AllLanguageModelSettings, resolving per-provider fields including custom headers via custom_headers_from.

nodes.name: anchor.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the multi-buffer Anchor type, a stable position that survives edits by binding a text::Anchor to a specific excerpt (or the Min/Max sentinels), plus the ExcerptAnchor and AnchorRangeExt helpers used to resolve anchors back into offsets and points against a snapshot.
nodes.languageNotes: Anchors are the linchpin of stable cursor/selection tracking across concurrent edits; comparison (cmp) resolves excerpt ordering then defers to the inner text anchor, and bias_left/bias_right control which side of an insertion the anchor sticks to.

nodes.name: Anchor
nodes.summary: A stable position in a MultiBuffer, either the Min/Max sentinel or an Excerpt-scoped anchor; provides ordering, bias adjustment, validity checks, and conversion to offsets/points via a snapshot.

nodes.name: ExcerptAnchor
nodes.summary: The excerpt-scoped variant of an anchor, wrapping a text::Anchor with its owning excerpt path and an optional diff-base anchor so positions inside deleted diff hunks can be resolved.

nodes.name: AnchorRangeExt
nodes.summary: Extension trait on Range<Anchor> adding ordering, containment, overlap, and offset/point conversion helpers for anchor ranges.

nodes.name: cmp
nodes.summary: Total ordering for ExcerptAnchor that compares excerpt locators first and falls back to the inner text-anchor comparison within the same excerpt, honoring Min/Max sentinels.

nodes.name: is_valid
nodes.summary: Checks whether an ExcerptAnchor still resolves against the given snapshot, verifying the excerpt exists and the underlying text anchor remains valid.

nodes.name: to_excerpt_anchor
nodes.summary: Lowers a MultiBuffer Anchor (including Min/Max sentinels) into a concrete ExcerptAnchor resolved against the snapshot.

nodes.name: bias_left
nodes.summary: Produces a copy of the anchor biased toward the left of its position so it stays attached to preceding text across insertions.

nodes.name: bias_right
nodes.summary: Produces a copy of the anchor biased toward the right of its position so it stays attached to following text across insertions.

nodes.name: multi_buffer.rs
nodes.summary: The core of the multi_buffer crate: MultiBuffer stitches one or more language::Buffers into a single virtually-contiguous editing surface built from Excerpts, exposing an immutable MultiBufferSnapshot for reads and driving edits, diff-hunk expansion, indent/syntax/diagnostic queries, and cursor iteration over a sum-tree of excerpts and diff transforms.
nodes.languageNotes: Built on Zed's SumTree for O(log n) positional queries; a MultiBufferCursor walks parallel excerpt and diff-transform trees to map multibuffer coordinates to buffer coordinates. Extensive newtype dimensions (MultiBufferOffset, BufferOffset, *Utf16) enforce coordinate-space correctness at the type level, and #[cfg(test)] random-mutation helpers support fuzz/property testing.

nodes.name: MultiBuffer
nodes.summary: GPUI entity that owns the mutable buffer/diff state, transaction History, and cached snapshot; the primary API for building, editing, and querying a multi-buffer, including diff-hunk expand/collapse and buffer-event synchronization.

nodes.name: MultiBufferSnapshot
nodes.summary: Immutable, cheaply-clonable read view of a multi-buffer at a point in time, exposing the full read API: text and chunk iteration, coordinate conversions, anchor resolution, indent/bracket/syntax/diagnostic queries, and diff-hunk enumeration.

nodes.name: Excerpt
nodes.summary: A contiguous slice of one underlying buffer that participates in the multi-buffer, holding its path key, buffer snapshot, range, and text summary; provides chunk iteration and anchor clipping within its bounds.
