nodes.name: MultiBufferCursor
nodes.summary: Walks the parallel excerpt and diff-transform sum-trees to seek and iterate multibuffer regions, mapping between multibuffer and per-buffer coordinate spaces while caching the current region.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Enum of events a MultiBuffer emits (edits, buffer add/remove, diff/diagnostics/language changes, transaction undone) that downstream views subscribe to.

nodes.name: MultiBufferDiffHunk
nodes.summary: Describes a diff hunk within the multi-buffer, carrying its row range, owning buffer, buffer/base byte ranges, status, and word-level diffs.

nodes.name: DiffTransform
nodes.summary: A node in the diff-transform sum-tree, representing either a run of buffer content or a deleted hunk to be shown; the mechanism by which expanded diffs are woven into multibuffer coordinates.

nodes.name: MBTextSummary
nodes.summary: Aggregatable text summary (lengths, line counts, longest row, utf16 metrics) used as the sum-tree summary type so positional and dimensional queries resolve in logarithmic time.

nodes.name: ExcerptSummary
nodes.summary: Sum-tree summary for the excerpt tree, tracking path key ordering, max anchor, widest line number, and aggregated text so excerpts can be located by position or key.

nodes.name: MultiBufferChunks
nodes.summary: Forward chunk iterator over a multibuffer range that splices together per-excerpt buffer chunks and diff-base chunks, optionally language-aware for syntax highlighting.

nodes.name: DiffState
nodes.summary: Tracks the BufferDiff attached to a buffer (or an inverted diff against a main buffer) plus its event subscription, and produces a snapshot for the read path.

nodes.name: edit_internal
nodes.summary: The central edit path: translates multibuffer-coordinate edits into per-buffer edits, applies autoindent, optionally coalesces adjacent edits, and drives the underlying buffers within the current transaction.

nodes.name: convert_edits_to_buffer_edits
nodes.summary: Maps a batch of multibuffer-coordinate edits onto the concrete per-buffer ranges and text they affect, resolving excerpt boundaries and preserving original indent columns.

nodes.name: sync_from_buffer_changes
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the multibuffer snapshot after underlying buffers change, recomputing excerpt edits and feeding them into diff-transform reconciliation to keep the virtual coordinate space consistent.

nodes.name: sync_diff_transforms
nodes.summary: Reconciles the diff-transform sum-tree against a set of excerpt edits and a change kind, deciding which deleted hunks to keep, expand, or drop.

nodes.name: recompute_diff_transforms_for_edit
nodes.summary: Recomputes the diff transforms spanning a single excerpt edit, interleaving surviving deleted hunks with new buffer content to produce the updated transform run.

nodes.name: expand_or_collapse_diff_hunks_inner
nodes.summary: Toggles expansion state of diff hunks intersecting the given ranges, updating the expanded-hunk set that governs how deleted lines are shown.

nodes.name: summary_for_anchor
nodes.summary: Resolves an anchor to its full dimensional summary (offset, point, utf16 variants) against the snapshot, accounting for diff transforms and deleted-hunk positioning.

nodes.name: anchor_at
nodes.summary: Creates a MultiBuffer anchor at a given position with the requested bias, locating the containing excerpt and binding to the underlying buffer's text anchor.

nodes.name: range_to_buffer_ranges
nodes.summary: Decomposes a multibuffer range into the list of per-buffer ranges (and their excerpts) it covers, the workhorse for routing reads and edits to underlying buffers.

nodes.name: diff_hunks_in_range
nodes.summary: Enumerates diff hunks intersecting a multibuffer range, mapping each buffer-level hunk into multibuffer rows and ranges with its status and word diffs.

nodes.name: lift_buffer_metadata
nodes.summary: Generic helper that lifts per-buffer metadata (diagnostics, brackets, runnables, etc.) intersecting a query range up into multibuffer coordinates via a supplied extractor callback.

nodes.name: excerpt_boundaries_in_range
nodes.summary: Yields the excerpt boundaries (header/footer transitions between buffers) that fall within a range, used to render multi-buffer section headers.

nodes.name: indent_guides_in_range
nodes.summary: Computes indentation guide segments for a range, honoring per-language settings and excerpt boundaries.

nodes.name: enclosing_indent
nodes.summary: Finds the indentation-defined block enclosing a target row by scanning outward across non-blank lines.

nodes.name: build_region
nodes.summary: Constructs the MultiBufferRegion for the cursor's current position, resolving which buffer, diff-hunk status, excerpt, and coordinate ranges apply.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Advances the MultiBufferBytes iterator, stitching buffer content and deleted-hunk bytes across excerpt and diff-transform boundaries.

nodes.name: check_invariants
nodes.summary: Debug/test-only consistency check that validates the excerpt tree, diff-transform tree, and coordinate mappings agree; a key aid for the randomized mutation tests.

nodes.name: randomly_mutate
nodes.summary: Test-support helper that applies a random sequence of edits and excerpt mutations, driving property/fuzz testing of the multibuffer.

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Deep-clones a MultiBuffer into a new GPUI context, re-subscribing to buffer and diff events so the copy stays live.

nodes.name: singleton
nodes.summary: Constructs a single-buffer multibuffer wrapping one Buffer in one full-span excerpt, the common case for an ordinary editor pane.

nodes.name: path_key.rs
nodes.summary: Defines PathKey, the sortable identity used to group and order excerpts by file path (with an optional sort prefix), and the MultiBuffer methods that set, merge, expand, and remove excerpt ranges for a given path or buffer.
nodes.languageNotes: PathKey lets a multi-buffer present excerpts grouped and ordered by file (e.g. search results or diagnostics views); update_path_excerpts is the heavy reconciliation routine that diffs desired vs existing excerpt ranges for a path.

nodes.name: PathKey
nodes.summary: Sortable key identifying and ordering a buffer's excerpts within a multi-buffer by path, with an optional sort prefix for custom grouping.

nodes.name: update_path_excerpts
nodes.summary: Core reconciliation routine that diffs the desired excerpt ranges for a path against the existing ones and applies the minimal set of insertions and removals to the excerpt tree.

nodes.name: expand_excerpts
nodes.summary: Expands the context lines around a set of anchored excerpts in a given direction, growing their ranges without duplicating overlapping regions.

nodes.name: remove_excerpts
nodes.summary: Removes the excerpts for a given path, cleaning up path-key indices and emitting the appropriate buffer-removed events.

nodes.name: merge_new_with_existing_excerpt_ranges
nodes.summary: Merges newly requested excerpt ranges with the ranges already present for a path, coalescing overlaps so a buffer isn't excerpted twice.

nodes.name: set_anchored_excerpts_for_path
nodes.summary: Sets the excerpts for a path from anchor-based ranges, resolving anchors against the buffer and applying the requested context line count.

nodes.name: update_excerpts_for_path
nodes.summary: Public entry for updating a path's excerpts from a set of ranges plus context lines, delegating to the merge and reconciliation routines.

nodes.name: transaction.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the MultiBuffer's undo/redo History: a stack of Transactions that each fan out to per-buffer transaction ids, with grouping by time interval, merging, and the MultiBuffer methods that begin/end transactions and drive undo/redo across all constituent buffers.
nodes.languageNotes: A single multibuffer transaction maps to a set of per-buffer transaction ids; group_interval-based auto-grouping coalesces rapid edits into one undo step, and undo/redo replay coordinates all affected buffers atomically.

nodes.name: History
nodes.summary: Undo/redo stacks of multibuffer transactions with time-based grouping; manages transaction ids, depth for nested transactions, and pop/merge/forget operations.

nodes.name: Transaction
nodes.summary: A single undo unit mapping the multibuffer transaction id to the set of per-buffer transaction ids it spans, with timing metadata and a grouping-suppression flag.

nodes.name: end_transaction
nodes.summary: Closes the open transaction, recording the per-buffer transactions it covered and pushing it onto the undo stack (or discarding it if empty).

nodes.name: push_transaction
nodes.summary: Pushes a completed transaction onto the undo stack, applying time-based grouping to coalesce with the previous transaction when within the group interval.

nodes.name: edited_ranges_for_transaction
nodes.summary: Collects the multibuffer ranges edited by a transaction by mapping each per-buffer edited range up through the excerpts, used to restore selections after undo/redo.

nodes.name: undo
nodes.summary: Pops the top undo transaction and replays its inverse across all constituent buffers, emitting the TransactionUndone event.

nodes.name: redo
nodes.summary: Pops the top redo transaction and re-applies it across all constituent buffers.

nodes.name: merge_transactions
nodes.summary: Merges one transaction's per-buffer transactions into a destination transaction, folding two undo steps into one.

nodes.name: end_transaction_with_source
nodes.summary: Ends the current multibuffer transaction attributing it to an edit source, ending the corresponding transactions on each affected buffer.

nodes.name: group_trailing
nodes.summary: Groups the last n transactions on the undo stack into a single undo unit.

nodes.name: batches.rs
nodes.summary: Client for the OpenAI Batch API: uploads JSONL batch input files, creates and retrieves batch jobs, and downloads/parses batch output results.

nodes.name: Batch
nodes.summary: Response payload representing an OpenAI batch job's status, timestamps, and result file references.

nodes.name: upload_batch_file
nodes.summary: Uploads a JSONL-formatted batch input file to OpenAI via multipart form data and returns the resulting FileObject.

nodes.name: create_batch
nodes.summary: Submits a CreateBatchRequest to OpenAI to start a new batch job against an uploaded input file.

nodes.name: retrieve_batch
nodes.summary: Fetches the current status and metadata of a previously created batch job by id.

nodes.name: download_file
nodes.summary: Downloads the raw content of an OpenAI file (e.g. a batch output file) by file id.

nodes.name: completion.rs
nodes.summary: Maps OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses API streaming events into Zed's unified language-model completion event format, handling tool calls, reasoning, and message deltas.
nodes.languageNotes: Two parallel event-mapper state machines (OpenAiEventMapper for Chat Completions, OpenAiResponseEventMapper for the newer Responses API) reconcile OpenAI's differing streaming formats into one internal event model.

nodes.name: OpenAiEventMapper
nodes.summary: Stateful mapper that converts a stream of OpenAI Chat Completions API events into Zed's internal LanguageModelCompletionEvent stream, tracking in-progress tool calls.

nodes.name: OpenAiResponseEventMapper
nodes.summary: Stateful mapper that converts a stream of OpenAI Responses API events (including reasoning and custom tool calls) into Zed's internal completion event stream.

nodes.name: map_event (Responses API, line 882)
nodes.summary: Translates a single OpenAI Responses API stream event into zero or more internal completion events, handling text deltas, tool calls, reasoning, and errors.

nodes.name: into_open_ai
nodes.summary: Converts a generic Zed LanguageModelRequest into an OpenAI Chat Completions API Request payload.

nodes.name: append_message_to_response_items
nodes.summary: Appends a Zed request message's content (text, images, tool calls/results) as one or more items in the OpenAI Responses API input item list.

nodes.name: into_open_ai_response
nodes.summary: Converts a generic Zed LanguageModelRequest into an OpenAI Responses API Request payload.

nodes.name: map_event (Chat Completions, line 703)
nodes.summary: Translates a single OpenAI Chat Completions API streaming choice/delta into internal completion events, accumulating partial tool calls.

nodes.name: handle_completion
nodes.summary: Top-level dispatcher that routes a completion request to either the Chat Completions or Responses API path based on the model's capabilities.

nodes.name: open_ai.rs
nodes.summary: Core OpenAI API crate module defining request/response types (Model, Request, ToolDefinition, Usage, etc.), the streaming and non-streaming chat completion functions, and the embeddings API client.
nodes.languageNotes: Central schema module (983 lines, 30 structs/enums) shared by batches.rs, completion.rs, and responses.rs; Model enum encodes per-model capability metadata (reasoning support, token limits, compaction).

nodes.name: Model
nodes.summary: Enum of supported OpenAI models with associated capability metadata: token limits, reasoning-effort support, and feature flags like parallel tool calls and compaction.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.summary: Request payload struct for the OpenAI Chat Completions API, including messages, tools, and sampling parameters.

nodes.name: stream_completion
nodes.summary: Issues a streaming Chat Completions request to the OpenAI API and returns an async stream of parsed ResponseStreamEvent items.

nodes.name: non_streaming_completion
nodes.summary: Issues a non-streaming Chat Completions request to the OpenAI API and returns the parsed Response.

nodes.name: supported_reasoning_efforts
nodes.summary: Returns the set of reasoning-effort levels supported by a given model, used to validate and populate reasoning configuration in requests.

nodes.name: embed
nodes.summary: Calls the OpenAI embeddings API for a batch of input texts and returns the resulting embedding vectors.

nodes.name: responses.rs
nodes.summary: Defines request/response/event types for OpenAI's newer Responses API (structured input items, reasoning, custom tools) and the streaming client function that calls it.
nodes.languageNotes: Responses API models a richer item-based conversation format (message, function-call, reasoning, custom-tool items) versus the flatter Chat Completions message array in open_ai.rs.

nodes.name: stream_response
nodes.summary: Issues a streaming request to the OpenAI Responses API endpoint and returns an async stream of parsed StreamEvent items, handling SSE parsing and error responses.

nodes.name: Request (Responses API)
nodes.summary: Request payload struct for the OpenAI Responses API, including structured input items, tool definitions, and reasoning configuration.

nodes.name: StreamEvent
nodes.summary: Enum of all possible Server-Sent Event payloads emitted by the OpenAI Responses API streaming endpoint.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: Defines RpcError and related traits for converting between Rust error types and the wire-protocol Error proto message, including error codes and tagged context.

nodes.name: RpcError
nodes.summary: Structured RPC error type carrying an error code, message, and optional tag, convertible to and from the wire protocol's Error message.

nodes.name: ErrorExt
nodes.summary: Extension trait adding error-code/tag introspection and anyhow-conversion helpers to generic error types used across the RPC layer.

nodes.name: to_proto
nodes.summary: Converts an application error into the wire-protocol Error message, encoding error code and tag metadata.

nodes.name: macros.rs
nodes.summary: Declares the messages! macro that generates EnvelopedMessage trait implementations and envelope-dispatch boilerplate for every RPC message type, plus a companion macro for request/response pairing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses macro_rules! to eliminate per-message boilerplate: given a list of (MessageName, Priority) pairs, it generates envelope conversion, dispatch, and trait impls for all of them at once.

nodes.name: proto.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the wire protocol: re-exports generated protobuf types, invokes the messages! macro to wire up all RPC message types, and provides helpers for splitting large worktree/repository updates into chunks and computing write-permission flags.
nodes.languageNotes: Central protocol definition module tying together error.rs, macros.rs, and typed_envelope.rs; splits oversized worktree/repository update messages to respect message-size limits over the wire.

nodes.name: split_worktree_update
nodes.summary: Splits a large UpdateWorktree message into multiple smaller chunks to stay under the RPC message size limit.

nodes.name: split_repository_update
nodes.summary: Splits a large repository update message into multiple smaller chunks to stay under the RPC message size limit.

nodes.name: query_name_and_write_permissions
nodes.summary: Computes a query's display name and derived write-permission flags for collaboration RPCs.

nodes.name: typed_envelope.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the core traits and types for typed RPC message envelopes: EnvelopedMessage, RequestMessage, TypedEnvelope, and the AnyTypedEnvelope dynamic-dispatch trait used to route incoming messages by sender and priority.

nodes.name: EnvelopedMessage
nodes.summary: Trait implemented by every RPC message type (via the messages! macro) providing its name, priority, and envelope conversion methods.

nodes.name: AnyTypedEnvelope
nodes.summary: Object-safe trait allowing dynamic dispatch over any typed envelope, exposing payload type id/name, sender info, and priority for generic RPC routing.

nodes.name: TypedEnvelope
nodes.summary: Generic wrapper pairing an RPC message payload with its envelope metadata (sender id, message id, receive timestamp).

nodes.name: LspRequestMessage
nodes.summary: Trait for RPC messages that wrap an LSP request, providing conversion to/from LSP request and response types over the proto layer.

nodes.name: into_response
nodes.summary: Converts a request message into its corresponding wire-protocol response envelope, used when replying to RPC requests.

nodes.name: linux_bubblewrap.rs
nodes.summary: Linux sandboxing backend that wraps subprocess invocations using bubblewrap (bwrap), building the sandbox argument list, seccomp filters, and a validation bridge socket for permission escalation checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a launcher/bridge process architecture: a privileged-adjacent bridge process validates filesystem access requests from the sandboxed child over a Unix socket protocol, using seccomp-based syscall interception.

nodes.name: SandboxPermissions
nodes.summary: Describes the filesystem and network permissions granted to a sandboxed process on Linux via bubblewrap.

nodes.name: ValidationFdSender
nodes.summary: Sends file descriptors over a Unix socket to the validation bridge process so it can validate and grant access to requested paths.

nodes.name: wrap_invocation
nodes.summary: Wraps a command invocation with the bubblewrap sandbox launcher, setting up validation sockets, seccomp filters, and bind mounts before spawning.

nodes.name: build_bwrap_args_with_sandbox_paths
nodes.summary: Constructs the full bwrap command-line argument list, including bind mounts, namespace flags, and permitted paths.

nodes.name: run_wsl_helper
nodes.summary: Runs the WSL helper process entry point that decodes launcher arguments and executes the sandboxed command inside a WSL environment.

nodes.name: build_command_seccomp_program
nodes.summary: Builds the seccomp-bpf program used to intercept and validate filesystem-related syscalls made by the sandboxed process.

nodes.name: run_bridge
nodes.summary: Runs the bridge process loop that receives validation requests from the sandboxed child and grants or denies filesystem access.

nodes.name: macos_seatbelt.rs
nodes.summary: macOS sandboxing backend that generates a Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) profile file from the requested permissions and wraps command invocations with it.
nodes.languageNotes: Generates Apple's Sandbox Profile Language (SBPL) text directly, escaping paths for safe embedding in the generated .sb config.

nodes.name: SeatbeltConfigFile
nodes.summary: Represents a generated temporary Seatbelt sandbox profile file used to constrain a wrapped subprocess on macOS.

nodes.name: generate_seatbelt_config
nodes.summary: Generates the full Sandbox Profile Language (SBPL) text granting the configured filesystem and network permissions for a sandboxed process on macOS.

nodes.name: wrap_invocation
nodes.summary: Wraps a command invocation with sandbox-exec using the generated Seatbelt profile.

nodes.name: sandbox.rs
nodes.summary: Cross-platform sandboxing crate root defining the Sandbox struct, filesystem/network policy types, and platform dispatch (wrap_linux/wrap_macos/wrap_windows) for running commands under OS-level sandboxing.
nodes.languageNotes: Central policy/dispatch module unifying the three OS-specific backends (bubblewrap, seatbelt, WSL); manages a restricted network proxy and per-platform sandbox capability probing.

nodes.name: Sandbox
nodes.summary: Top-level sandbox handle that holds filesystem/network policy and dispatches command wrapping to the appropriate OS-specific backend.

nodes.name: SandboxPolicy
nodes.summary: Combined filesystem and network policy describing what a sandboxed process is permitted to access.

nodes.name: GrantableWriteDir
nodes.summary: Represents a directory that can be dynamically granted write access within the sandbox, with path canonicalization and finalize/discard lifecycle.

nodes.name: wrap_linux
nodes.summary: Dispatches command wrapping to the Linux bubblewrap backend based on the sandbox's configured policy.

nodes.name: wrap_macos
nodes.summary: Dispatches command wrapping to the macOS Seatbelt backend based on the sandbox's configured policy.

nodes.name: wrap_windows
nodes.summary: Dispatches command wrapping to the WSL-based Windows sandbox backend based on the sandbox's configured policy.

nodes.name: linux_location_is_equal_or_descendant
nodes.summary: Determines whether one host filesystem location is equal to or a descendant of another, used to merge and deduplicate policy paths on Linux.

nodes.name: ensure_restricted_proxy
nodes.summary: Starts a restricted local proxy server used to enforce the sandbox's network access policy for outbound connections.

nodes.name: windows_wsl.rs
nodes.summary: Windows sandboxing backend that runs sandboxed commands inside WSL, translating Windows paths to WSL paths, probing the WSL environment, and forwarding filtered environment variables into the sandboxed bubblewrap invocation.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges Windows and Linux sandboxing by shelling out to WSL and reusing the bubblewrap backend inside it; includes bidirectional Windows<->WSL path mapping and caching.

nodes.name: WslSandboxUnavailable
nodes.summary: Error type describing why WSL-based sandboxing could not be used on the current system.

nodes.name: wrap_invocation
nodes.summary: Wraps a command invocation for execution inside WSL, resolving paths, selecting a distro, and delegating to the bubblewrap sandbox within the Linux subsystem.

nodes.name: ensure_wsl_zed_helper
nodes.summary: Ensures the Zed WSL helper binary is present and up to date inside the target WSL distro, copying it in if necessary.

nodes.name: build_bwrap_args
nodes.summary: Builds bubblewrap arguments for the WSL-hosted sandbox invocation, mapping resolved WSL paths into bind-mount arguments.

nodes.name: probe_environment
nodes.summary: Probes the target WSL distro's environment (available tools, paths) needed to run the sandbox helper.

nodes.name: resolve_uncached_paths
nodes.summary: Resolves Windows filesystem paths to their WSL equivalents for entries not already present in the path-mapping cache.

nodes.name: components.rs
nodes.summary: Tiny module file that re-exports the settings UI's reusable component submodules (currently just a stub aggregator).

nodes.name: pages.rs
nodes.summary: Declares the ordered list of top-level settings pages (general, appearance, editor, AI, etc.) shown in the settings UI navigation sidebar.

nodes.name: page_data.rs
nodes.summary: Very large data-definition file (~10.6k lines) that declares the content and field layout of every settings page (general, appearance, keymap, editor, languages, search, window/layout, panels, debugger, terminal, version control, collaboration, AI, network) plus per-language settings sections used to render the GPUI settings window.
nodes.languageNotes: Each `*_page` function builds a declarative tree of SettingsPageItem/SettingField descriptors for one settings category; the file is almost entirely declarative data rather than control flow, which is why line count is high but cyclomatic complexity per function is low.

nodes.name: settings_ui.rs
nodes.summary: Main settings_ui crate module (~6.8k lines) implementing the GPUI settings editor window: navigation sidebar, search/filtering, per-page rendering, settings-file targeting (user/project/server), and field renderers (text, toggle, dropdown, font/theme pickers).
nodes.languageNotes: Central struct SettingsWindow owns ~60 methods covering navigation, search-index building, sub-page stacking, and rendering; most of the file's 127 top-level functions are actually its impl methods.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Crate initialization entry point that registers the settings UI actions and wires up renderer registration for the settings window.

nodes.name: init_renderers
nodes.summary: Registers the field-renderer implementations (text, toggle, dropdown, picker, etc.) for each setting value type so the generic settings window can render arbitrary fields.

nodes.name: open_settings_editor
nodes.summary: Action handler that opens the settings editor window, the primary user-facing entry point into the settings UI.

nodes.name: open_settings_editor_to_page
nodes.summary: Opens the settings editor window and navigates directly to a specific settings page, used for deep-linking into settings from elsewhere in the app.

nodes.name: open_settings_editor_at_target
nodes.summary: Opens the settings editor targeted at a specific settings file (user, project, or server), pre-selecting the correct file scope.

nodes.name: open_settings_editor_with
nodes.summary: Lower-level constructor that builds and opens a settings editor window with custom navigation and file-target parameters.

nodes.name: render_page
nodes.summary: Renders the full content area for the currently selected settings page, laying out its sections and fields as GPUI elements.

nodes.name: render_nav
nodes.summary: Renders the settings window's left-hand navigation sidebar, including search results, page list, and highlighted matches.

nodes.name: build_search_index
nodes.summary: Builds an in-memory search index over all settings page items so the settings window can support fuzzy search across settings.

nodes.name: update_matches
nodes.summary: Recomputes and highlights search match indices against the settings search index as the user types a query.

nodes.name: render_files_header
nodes.summary: Renders the header row listing which settings files (user/project/server) are available and currently selected in the settings window.

nodes.name: open_current_settings_file
nodes.summary: Opens the raw JSON/TOML settings file backing the currently selected settings scope in a text editor, for advanced manual edits.

nodes.name: navigate_to_sub_page
nodes.summary: Pushes a new sub-page onto the settings window's navigation stack, used for drilling into nested settings sections.

nodes.name: navigate_to_setting
nodes.summary: Navigates the settings window directly to a specific individual setting field, scrolling it into view.

nodes.name: update_settings_file
nodes.summary: Applies an edit to the underlying settings file content and persists it, propagating the change back into the live settings state.

nodes.name: render_dropdown
nodes.summary: Field renderer that draws a dropdown/select control bound to an enum-valued setting field.

nodes.name: render_theme_picker
nodes.summary: Field renderer that draws the theme picker control, listing available themes and applying the selected theme to the setting.

nodes.name: SettingsWindow
nodes.summary: Central GPUI view struct for the settings editor window; owns navigation state, the search index, sub-page stack, and the ~60 methods that build and render the entire settings UI.

nodes.name: AnySettingField
nodes.summary: Type-erased trait/wrapper representing a settings field of any concrete type, exposing common operations like reset-to-default and JSON-path lookup used by the generic renderer pipeline.

nodes.name: SettingFieldRenderer
nodes.summary: Registry mapping setting field types to their rendering functions, populated by init_renderers and consulted when drawing settings pages.

nodes.name: SubPage
nodes.summary: Represents a single entry on the settings window's sub-page navigation stack (e.g. a drilled-down settings section).

nodes.name: SettingsPageItem
nodes.summary: Enum/struct representing a single renderable item within a settings page (a header, a field, or a link), the unit rendered by render_page.

nodes.name: SettingsUiFile
nodes.summary: Represents one addressable settings file target (user, a specific project/worktree, or a remote server) that the settings window can display and edit.

nodes.name: ProjectSettingsUpdateQueue
nodes.summary: Queues and sequences pending edits to project-level settings files so concurrent field updates don't race when writing to disk.

nodes.name: settings_data
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that assembles the full list of settings pages by calling each page-builder function, forming the data backbone consumed by the settings window.

nodes.name: developer_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page listing developer/diagnostic options.

nodes.name: general_page
nodes.summary: Builds the general settings page covering app-wide preferences such as telemetry, restore behavior, and startup options.

nodes.name: appearance_page
nodes.summary: Builds the appearance settings page covering themes, fonts, icon themes, and UI scaling options.

nodes.name: keymap_page
nodes.summary: Builds the keymap settings page for viewing and configuring keybindings.

nodes.name: editor_page
nodes.summary: Builds the large editor settings page covering text editing behavior: formatting, indentation, cursor, whitespace, code actions, and related options.

nodes.name: languages_and_tools_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for per-language tooling configuration such as formatters, linters, and language servers.

nodes.name: search_and_files_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for search behavior and file-handling preferences (exclusions, file scanning, etc.).

nodes.name: window_and_layout_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page controlling window chrome, pane layout, and workspace arrangement options.

nodes.name: panels_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for configuring individual UI panels (project panel, outline panel, etc.) and their display options.

nodes.name: debugger_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for debugger configuration options.

nodes.name: terminal_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for integrated terminal configuration (shell, font, cursor, environment).

nodes.name: version_control_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for version control (git) integration options.

nodes.name: collaboration_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for collaboration/multiplayer session options.

nodes.name: ai_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for AI/agent features, including model selection and agent behavior options.

nodes.name: network_page
nodes.summary: Builds the settings page for network/proxy configuration options.

nodes.name: language_settings_data
nodes.summary: Builds the shared field layout for per-language editor settings (used both globally and per-language override sections), the single largest function in the file.

nodes.name: non_editor_language_settings_data
nodes.summary: Builds the field layout for per-language settings that fall outside the core editor behavior category (e.g. formatter/linter selection per language).

nodes.name: edit_prediction_language_settings_section
nodes.summary: Builds the per-language edit-prediction (AI code completion) settings section.

nodes.name: extension_snippet.rs
nodes.summary: Wires the snippet subsystem into the extension host by registering a SnippetRegistryProxy that forwards extension-supplied snippet files into the global SnippetRegistry.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements an ExtensionHostProxy trait so extensions can contribute snippets without depending on the concrete registry.

nodes.name: format.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the VS Code snippet file format as Serde-deserializable types (VsSnippetsFile, VsCodeSnippet, ListOrDirect) and generates a JSON schema for editor validation of user snippet files.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses schemars to emit a draft-2019-09 JSON schema; ListOrDirect models VS Code's convention where a field may be either a single value or a list.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root providing SnippetProvider, a GPUI entity that watches the user's snippets directory on the filesystem, parses VS Code snippet files, and resolves snippets by language for editor completion, merging in extension- and user-registered snippets.
nodes.languageNotes: Built on GPUI's Entity/Context model with async filesystem watching via futures streams; uses const-generic lookup_snippets::<DEDUP> to toggle deduplication.

nodes.name: registry.rs
nodes.summary: Global, thread-safe SnippetRegistry storing snippets registered outside the filesystem watcher (chiefly from extensions), keyed by language kind behind an RwLock.
nodes.languageNotes: Installed as a GPUI global via a GlobalSnippetRegistry newtype wrapping an Arc; interior mutability through parking_lot RwLock.

nodes.name: VsSnippetsFile
nodes.summary: Deserializable representation of an entire VS Code snippets file: a map from snippet name to VsCodeSnippet, with a custom JSON schema for editor validation.

nodes.name: VsCodeSnippet
nodes.summary: Single snippet entry as authored in a VS Code snippets file, holding optional prefix(es), the body text, and an optional description.

nodes.name: generate_json_schema
nodes.summary: Builds a draft-2019-09 JSON schema for the snippets file format, applying transforms that deny unknown fields and allow trailing commas.

nodes.name: file_to_snippets
nodes.summary: Converts a parsed VsSnippetsFile into an iterator of validated Snippet values, resolving default prefixes and reporting parse errors per snippet.

nodes.name: Snippet
nodes.summary: Fully-resolved snippet with its name, prefixes, body, and optional description, as consumed by the editor's completion machinery.

nodes.name: process_updates
nodes.summary: Async handler that reacts to filesystem change events, loading, parsing, and indexing (or removing) snippet files by language kind within the SnippetProvider entity.

nodes.name: initial_scan
nodes.summary: Performs the first-pass directory read of a watched snippets folder and feeds all discovered entries through process_updates.

nodes.name: SnippetProvider
nodes.summary: GPUI entity that owns the filesystem handle, the language-keyed snippet index, and the directory-watch tasks; primary API for resolving snippets for a given language.

nodes.name: watch_directory
nodes.summary: Spawns a long-lived background task that runs the initial scan then streams filesystem watch events into process_updates for one snippets directory.

nodes.name: lookup_snippets
nodes.summary: Const-generic resolver that gathers snippets for a language from the local index, the global user watcher, and the extension registry, optionally deduplicating results.

nodes.name: snippets_for
nodes.summary: Public entry point that returns the merged, deduplicated set of language-specific and global snippets for the requested language.

nodes.name: SnippetRegistry
nodes.summary: Thread-safe, language-keyed store of externally-registered snippets, exposed as a GPUI global and populated by extensions through register_snippets.

nodes.name: register_snippets
nodes.summary: Parses a raw snippets file's contents, converts entries via file_to_snippets, and stores the resulting snippets under the language kind derived from the file stem.

nodes.name: sum_tree.rs
nodes.summary: Core implementation of SumTree, a persistent B-tree-like data structure that stores items annotated with an associative summary, used throughout the codebase (e.g. rope/text buffers) for efficient indexed lookup and range queries.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements copy-on-write persistence via Arc-shared nodes and a generic Summary/Dimension trait system so callers can index the tree by arbitrary derived metrics (e.g. byte offset, line count).

nodes.name: cursor.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Cursor and FilterCursor, stateful traversal objects that walk a SumTree forward/backward and seek to positions defined by a target Dimension, forming the primary read API for the tree.

nodes.name: tree_map.rs
nodes.summary: Implements TreeMap and TreeSet, ordered key-value/key-only collections built on top of SumTree, providing a BTreeMap-like API with persistent/cheap-clone semantics.

nodes.name: property_test.rs
nodes.summary: Property-based test module for SumTree, exercising tree invariants under randomized sequences of operations.

nodes.name: from_iter
nodes.summary: Builds a SumTree from a sequential iterator of items, constructing balanced internal nodes in one pass.

nodes.name: from_par_iter
nodes.summary: Builds a SumTree from a parallel iterator, using multiple threads to construct subtrees before merging them.

nodes.name: find_exact
nodes.summary: Searches the tree for an item matching a target dimension exactly, returning None if no exact match exists.

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Searches the tree for an item at or near a target dimension, honoring the given seek bias.

nodes.name: find_iterate
nodes.summary: Internal iterative helper implementing the tree-descent logic used by find, walking node children based on cumulative summaries.

nodes.name: find_with_prev
nodes.summary: Searches for an item at a target dimension while also tracking the previous item's summary, used for range-adjacent queries.

nodes.name: find_with_prev_iterate
nodes.summary: Internal iterative helper implementing the descent logic for find_with_prev.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Returns a FilterCursor that only yields items whose subtree summaries pass a caller-supplied predicate, enabling efficient sparse iteration.

nodes.name: push
nodes.summary: Appends a single item to the end of the tree, rebalancing nodes as needed.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Concatenates another SumTree onto the end of this one.

nodes.name: push_tree_recursive
nodes.summary: Core recursive algorithm for merging two trees together while maintaining B-tree balance invariants, the workhorse behind append.

nodes.name: append_large
nodes.summary: Specialized merge path for appending a much larger tree, avoiding degenerate rebalancing costs.

nodes.name: merge_into_right
nodes.summary: Merges a small tree into a large tree's rightmost path, part of the balanced tree-merge algorithm.

nodes.name: from_child_trees
nodes.summary: Constructs a new internal node from two child subtrees, computing the combined summary.

nodes.name: insert_or_replace
nodes.summary: Inserts an item into a keyed tree, replacing any existing item with the same key.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes the item matching a key from a keyed tree.

nodes.name: edit
nodes.summary: Applies a batch of insert/remove edits to a keyed tree in a single pass.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up an item by key in a keyed tree.

nodes.name: Summary
nodes.summary: Trait defining how per-item summaries combine associatively, the core abstraction that lets SumTree support arbitrary aggregate queries (counts, offsets, etc.).

nodes.name: Dimension
nodes.summary: Trait for projecting a Summary down to a specific queryable dimension (e.g. byte offset), used by Cursor::seek to navigate the tree.

nodes.name: SeekAggregate
nodes.summary: Accumulator used during a cursor seek to build up a summary or slice of the tree as it walks past leaves and items.

nodes.name: search_backward
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor backward through the tree until a caller-supplied predicate over node summaries becomes true, then descends to the exact item.

nodes.name: search_forward
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor forward through the tree until a caller-supplied predicate over node summaries becomes true, then descends to the exact item.

nodes.name: seek_internal
nodes.summary: Core cursor-seek algorithm that descends the tree toward a target Dimension using the given bias, the primary engine behind all cursor positioning operations.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up a value by key in the TreeMap.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a key-value pair from the TreeMap by key.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Updates the value at a key in place using a caller-supplied closure.

nodes.name: retain
nodes.summary: Removes all entries that don't satisfy a caller-supplied predicate.

nodes.name: insert_tree
nodes.summary: Merges another TreeMap's entries into this one.

nodes.name: zlog.rs
nodes.summary: Main module of the zlog logging crate: defines the Logger/Zlog global logging facade, scoped loggers, a Timer utility for measuring and logging durations, and crate initialization (init/try_init/init_test).

nodes.name: filter.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the ScopeMap log-scope filtering engine, resolving per-module/per-scope log level enablement from settings and environment configuration, with live refresh support.

nodes.name: sink.rs
nodes.summary: Implements log output sinks (stdout, stderr, rotating file) that format and write Record values, including file-size-based log rotation.

nodes.name: env_config.rs
nodes.summary: Parses the ZED_LOG-style environment variable syntax into an EnvFilter describing per-scope log level overrides.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Top-level global logging entry point that dispatches a log record to the configured sink after checking scope/level filtering.

nodes.name: scoped_logger
nodes.summary: Creates a child Logger scoped under a parent, used to build hierarchical logging scopes (e.g. crate::module::submodule).

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Completes a Timer by computing elapsed duration, emitting a warning log if it exceeded a configured threshold, and logging the final timing record.

nodes.name: Zlog
nodes.summary: Global logger implementation providing enabled/log/flush operations, the root of the zlog logging facade.

nodes.name: Logger
nodes.summary: A scoped logger handle bound to a specific module/scope string, used by call sites to emit log records tagged with their origin.

nodes.name: Timer
nodes.summary: RAII-style timer that logs a warning if a scoped operation exceeds a duration threshold, and logs its elapsed time on completion or drop.

nodes.name: is_scope_enabled
nodes.summary: Determines whether a given scope/module path is enabled at a given log level by walking up the scope hierarchy in the ScopeMap.

nodes.name: refresh_from_settings
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the active log filter configuration from the app's live settings, allowing log levels to be changed without restarting.

nodes.name: new_from_settings_and_env
nodes.summary: Builds a ScopeMap by merging settings-provided scope filters with environment-variable overrides and default filters, the core filter-construction algorithm.

nodes.name: is_enabled
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given scope and level pass the ScopeMap's filter rules, the hot-path check called on every log invocation.

nodes.name: ScopeMap
nodes.summary: Tree-structured map of scope names to enabled log levels, the central data structure used to decide whether a given log call site is active.

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Formats and writes a log Record to the configured sink (stdout/stderr/file), handling formatting, coloring, and rotation checks.

nodes.name: init_output_file
nodes.summary: Initializes the file-based log sink, opening or creating the log file at the given path with optional rotation.

nodes.name: open_or_create_log_file
nodes.summary: Opens the log file for appending, creating it and rotating an existing oversized file if necessary.

nodes.name: rotate_log_file
nodes.summary: Rotates the current log file to a backup path when it exceeds the configured maximum size.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses a ZED_LOG-style environment variable string into an EnvFilter mapping scopes to log levels.

nodes.name: parse_level
nodes.summary: Parses a single log-level token (e.g. 'debug', 'trace') from the environment filter string into a LevelFilter enum value.

nodes.name: agent_servers.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root defining the AgentServer trait (the common interface for spawnable external AI agent processes) and AgentServerDelegate, plus proxy-environment-variable loading used when launching agent subprocesses.

nodes.name: acp.rs
nodes.summary: Large module (~5k lines) implementing the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) connection layer: spawning agent subprocesses over stdio, session lifecycle (create/load/resume/close), prompt/notification handling, terminal and file-access permission requests, and debug message logging.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the client side of the ACP JSON-RPC protocol over stdio; AcpConnection is the central actor coordinating many concurrent sessions against a single agent subprocess.

nodes.name: custom.rs
nodes.summary: Implements CustomAgentServer, an AgentServer backed by a user-configured command line (custom ACP-speaking agent binary), including config-option handling and Gemini CLI API-key/registry-agent detection helpers.

nodes.name: load_proxy_env
nodes.summary: Loads HTTP(S)_PROXY-style environment variables to forward into spawned agent subprocesses.

nodes.name: AgentServer
nodes.summary: Trait defining the common interface every external AI agent integration implements: connecting, default modes/config options, and favorite-option toggling.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Spawns the configured custom agent command as a subprocess and establishes an ACP connection to it, implementing AgentServer::connect for CustomAgentServer.

nodes.name: toggle_favorite_config_option_value
nodes.summary: Toggles whether a given config option value is marked as a user favorite for quick access in the agent UI.

nodes.name: set_default_config_option
nodes.summary: Sets the default value for a named config option on the custom agent.

nodes.name: favorite_config_option_value_ids
nodes.summary: Returns the set of config option value IDs the user has marked as favorites for this custom agent.

nodes.name: is_registry_agent
nodes.summary: Checks whether the custom agent's command matches a known registry (built-in) agent, used to apply special-cased behavior.

nodes.name: CustomAgentServer
nodes.summary: AgentServer implementation for a user-defined external agent command, wrapping process spawning and config-option handling with the standard AgentServer trait.

nodes.name: stdio
nodes.summary: Spawns an agent subprocess and establishes an ACP JSON-RPC connection over its stdio pipes, the largest and central function in the file wiring up request/notification routing.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Public entry point that connects to an agent server and returns an AcpConnection, delegating to stdio for the actual subprocess/protocol setup.

nodes.name: handle_session_notification
nodes.summary: Handles incoming session-update notifications from the agent subprocess, dispatching them to update the relevant session's state (messages, tool calls, plans).

nodes.name: open_or_create_session
nodes.summary: Finds an existing session for a project/directory or creates a new one via the agent's session-creation protocol call.

nodes.name: apply_default_config_options
nodes.summary: Applies the agent's default configuration options (mode, model, etc.) to a newly created or loaded session.

nodes.name: new_session
nodes.summary: Sends the ACP new-session request to the agent subprocess and constructs the local AcpSession state to track it.

nodes.name: prompt
nodes.summary: Sends a user prompt to the agent for a given session over the ACP protocol and awaits the response.

nodes.name: close_session
nodes.summary: Terminates and cleans up an active agent session's local tracking state.

nodes.name: resume_session
nodes.summary: Resumes a previously loaded session, re-establishing local state for continued interaction.

nodes.name: load_session
nodes.summary: Loads a previously persisted session from the agent, requesting its history and current state.

nodes.name: handle_create_elicitation
nodes.summary: Handles the agent's elicitation request (a structured prompt asking the user to fill in additional information), presenting it to the user.

nodes.name: handle_request_permission
nodes.summary: Handles the agent's request for permission to perform a sensitive action (e.g. file write, command execution), routing it to the user for approval.

nodes.name: handle_create_terminal
nodes.summary: Handles the agent's request to create a terminal for running a command, allocating a local terminal instance.

nodes.name: mcp_servers_for_project
nodes.summary: Resolves the set of MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers configured for the current project, to advertise to the connected agent.

nodes.name: connect_client_future
nodes.summary: Builds the async future that drives the ACP client-side connection loop, processing incoming messages until the connection closes.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses a raw debug/log message into a structured AcpDebugMessage for display in the agent debug panel.

nodes.name: list_sessions
nodes.summary: Returns the list of currently tracked sessions for an agent connection.

nodes.name: AcpConnection
nodes.summary: Central actor representing a live connection to an agent subprocess; owns the session list, config state, and the ~31 methods that implement session lifecycle, prompting, and protocol callback handling.

nodes.name: AcpSessionList
nodes.summary: Tracks all active sessions for an agent connection, keyed by session ID, with lookup/insert/remove operations.

nodes.name: AcpDebugLog
nodes.summary: Buffers recent raw protocol messages for display in the agent connection debug panel.

nodes.name: SessionDirectories
nodes.summary: Tracks the mapping between agent sessions and the working directories they were created for, used to route file-system requests.

nodes.name: AcpConnectionDefaults
nodes.summary: Holds the default mode/config-option values applied to new sessions on an AcpConnection.

nodes.name: agent_settings.rs
nodes.summary: Defines AgentSettings, the top-level configuration struct for the AI agent panel (layout, model selection, auto-compact behavior, sandbox/tool permission rules, hardcoded security rule checks), plus the settings-parsing logic that compiles raw JSON settings into typed permission and regex-rule structures.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes a hardcoded security-rule layer (check_hardcoded_security_rules, expand_rm_to_single_path_commands) that pattern-matches potentially dangerous shell commands independent of user-configured sandbox permissions.

nodes.name: agent_profile.rs
nodes.summary: Defines AgentProfile and AgentProfileSettings, representing named tool-permission profiles for the AI agent (e.g. which tools/context-servers are enabled), including creation and persistence of custom profiles.

nodes.name: user_agents_md.rs
nodes.summary: Loads and watches the user's AGENTS.md file (custom instructions for AI agents), exposing its content and any read errors as reactive global state.

nodes.name: from_settings
nodes.summary: Converts raw deserialized settings content into a fully compiled AgentSettings value, resolving permission rules and regex patterns.

nodes.name: compile_sandbox_permissions
nodes.summary: Compiles the user's sandbox permission settings into a structured SandboxPermissions value used to gate agent tool execution.

nodes.name: compile_tool_permissions
nodes.summary: Compiles per-tool permission rules from settings into a ToolPermissions structure consulted before allowing an agent tool call.

nodes.name: compile_regex_rules
nodes.summary: Compiles a list of raw regex pattern strings from settings into validated CompiledRegex rules, reporting invalid patterns.

nodes.name: check_hardcoded_security_rules
nodes.summary: Checks a tool invocation's extracted commands against built-in (non-configurable) security rules, blocking known-dangerous patterns regardless of user permission settings.

nodes.name: expand_rm_to_single_path_commands
nodes.summary: Expands a shell `rm` command with multiple path arguments into individual single-path commands so each target can be checked against permission rules separately.

nodes.name: matches_hardcoded_patterns
nodes.summary: Checks whether a command string matches any of a set of hardcoded dangerous-command patterns.

nodes.name: normalize_path
nodes.summary: Normalizes a raw filesystem path string (resolving relative segments) for consistent comparison in security rule checks.

nodes.name: temperature_for_model
nodes.summary: Looks up the configured sampling temperature override for a given language model, falling back to a default.

nodes.name: language_model_to_selection
nodes.summary: Converts a resolved language model reference into the LanguageModelSelection settings representation used to persist the user's model choice.

nodes.name: get_layout
nodes.summary: Reads the current agent panel layout (agent vs editor mode) from settings.

nodes.name: set_layout
nodes.summary: Writes a new agent panel layout choice to settings, persisting the user's preference.

nodes.name: write_diff_to
nodes.summary: Writes only the fields of PanelLayout that differ from the currently merged settings, minimizing the diff written to the settings file.

nodes.name: parse_auto_compact_threshold
nodes.summary: Parses the raw auto-compact-threshold setting value (e.g. token count or percentage) into a typed AutoCompactThreshold.

nodes.name: AgentSettings
nodes.summary: Top-level settings struct for the AI agent panel, exposing enabled state, model temperature, layout, and other agent-wide preferences.

nodes.name: PanelLayout
nodes.summary: Represents the agent panel's layout mode (agent-focused vs editor-focused) and how it merges/diffs against settings files.

nodes.name: SandboxPermissions
nodes.summary: Compiled representation of the user's sandbox permission configuration, consulted before allowing agent-initiated command execution.

nodes.name: ToolPermissions
nodes.summary: Compiled per-tool permission rules, with validation for detecting invalid regex patterns supplied by the user.

nodes.name: CompiledRegex
nodes.summary: Wraps a compiled regular expression with the source pattern, used for permission-rule matching with graceful handling of invalid patterns.

nodes.name: AgentProfileId
nodes.summary: Newtype identifier for an agent tool-permission profile, referenced from AgentSettings and agent_profile.rs.

nodes.name: WindowLayout
nodes.summary: Represents the combined agent/editor window layout configuration used when computing the effective PanelLayout.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a new named agent profile derived from a base profile and persists it to settings.

nodes.name: save_to_settings
nodes.summary: Persists an AgentProfileSettings value back into the settings file content.

nodes.name: is_unmodified_default
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given profile ID still matches its unmodified built-in default configuration.

nodes.name: from
nodes.summary: Converts raw agent profile settings content into an AgentProfileSettings value.

nodes.name: AgentProfile
nodes.summary: Represents a named tool-permission profile for the AI agent, with lookup of the available profiles list.

nodes.name: AgentProfileSettings
nodes.summary: Settings representation of a single agent profile, including per-tool and per-context-server enablement, with default-detection and persistence helpers.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initializes the global UserAgentsMd state and starts the file watcher for AGENTS.md.

nodes.name: spawn_watcher
nodes.summary: Spawns a background task that watches the AGENTS.md file for changes and updates the reactive global state on modification.

nodes.name: probe_read_error
nodes.summary: Reads AGENTS.md and classifies any I/O error encountered, used to surface actionable error state to the UI.

nodes.name: UserAgentsMd
nodes.summary: Global handle exposing the current content and error state of the user's AGENTS.md file as reactive state.

nodes.name: UserAgentsMdState
nodes.summary: Holds the parsed content and any read error for the AGENTS.md file, the payload wrapped by UserAgentsMd.

nodes.name: anthropic.rs
nodes.summary: Core Anthropic API client crate root defining model catalog metadata, the full Messages API request/response wire types, streaming and non-streaming completion functions, rate-limit header parsing, and error mapping from Anthropic API errors into the app's generic completion error types.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive use of serde tagged enums to mirror Anthropic's Messages API JSON schema (content blocks, streaming events, tool use) and header-based rate-limit parsing via typed structs.

nodes.name: batches.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Anthropic Message Batches API: creating a batch, retrieving batch status, and downloading batch results (JSONL) with typed request/response structs.

nodes.name: completion.rs
nodes.summary: Converts the app's provider-agnostic LanguageModelCompletion request/event types into Anthropic's Messages API request format and back, including prompt-cache-control insertion and streaming event-to-completion-event mapping.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a stateful AnthropicEventMapper that accumulates streaming tool-use JSON deltas across events before emitting complete tool-call events.

nodes.name: from_listed
nodes.summary: Builds a Model definition from a ListModelEntry returned by the /models API, deriving thinking/effort/image capabilities and fast-mode/compaction beta headers.

nodes.name: list_models
nodes.summary: Fetches the list of available Anthropic models from the API and converts each entry into a Model via from_listed.

nodes.name: non_streaming_completion
nodes.summary: Sends a non-streaming completion request to Anthropic and parses the JSON response, handling error responses via handle_error_response.

nodes.name: send_request
nodes.summary: Builds and sends the raw HTTP POST request to the Anthropic Messages endpoint with auth and beta headers, returning the response plus parsed rate-limit info.

nodes.name: handle_error_response
nodes.summary: Reads an error HTTP response body and converts it into a typed AnthropicError, attaching parsed rate-limit info when available.

nodes.name: stream_completion_with_rate_limit_info
nodes.summary: Sends a streaming completion request and returns a boxed stream of parsed SSE Events alongside the initial rate-limit info, decoding 'data:' lines as JSON.

nodes.name: completion_error_from_anthropic_api
nodes.summary: Maps an Anthropic ApiError (by error code) into the app's generic language-model-core Error enum, including prompt-too-long token count extraction.

nodes.name: Model
nodes.summary: Describes a single Anthropic model's identity, token limits, thinking/effort/image capabilities and derived beta headers.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.summary: Serializable Anthropic Messages API request body including messages, tools, thinking config, cache control, and sampling parameters.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: Deserialized non-streaming Anthropic Messages API response including content blocks, stop reason and usage.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Tagged enum of Anthropic SSE streaming event variants (message start/stop, content block deltas, ping, error).

nodes.name: AnthropicError
nodes.summary: Error enum covering request serialization, HTTP transport, response parsing, rate limiting and server overload failures for the Anthropic client.

nodes.name: create_batch
nodes.summary: Submits a new Message Batch to the Anthropic Batches API and parses the resulting MessageBatch status object.

nodes.name: retrieve_batch
nodes.summary: Fetches the current status of a previously submitted message batch by ID.

nodes.name: retrieve_batch_results
nodes.summary: Downloads and parses the JSONL results file for a completed message batch into a list of per-request results.

nodes.name: MessageBatch
nodes.summary: Represents the status and metadata of a message batch job returned by the Anthropic Batches API.

nodes.name: into_anthropic
nodes.summary: Converts the generic LanguageModelCompletionRequest into an Anthropic-specific Request, applying model defaults, thinking/effort configuration, and prompt cache-control markers.

nodes.name: to_anthropic_content
nodes.summary: Maps a single generic message content block (text, thinking, image, tool use/result) into Anthropic's RequestContent representation.

nodes.name: map_event
nodes.summary: Translates a single Anthropic streaming Event into zero or more generic completion events, accumulating tool-use JSON deltas and tracking usage/stop reason state.

nodes.name: AnthropicEventMapper
nodes.summary: Stateful mapper that converts a stream of Anthropic SSE events into the app's generic LanguageModelCompletionEvent stream.

nodes.name: audio.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the audio subsystem: declares global audio constants (48kHz sample rate, stereo, 30s replay window), re-exports the pipeline and settings modules, and defines the Sound enum of built-in UI/call sound effects.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses rodio's nz! macro for compile-time NonZero sample-rate/channel constants; barrel module pattern with pub use re-exports.

nodes.name: Sound
nodes.summary: Enum of built-in sound effects (Joined, Mute, Unmute, screenshare start/stop, AgentDone, etc.) whose file() method maps each variant to a static asset basename for lookup by the audio pipeline.
nodes.languageNotes: Copy + Hash + Eq enum usable as a cache key; variants are inherited from Zed's collab feature set (call join/leave, screenshare).

nodes.name: audio_pipeline.rs
nodes.summary: Core audio engine built on rodio: enumerates and resolves input/output devices, opens capture/playback streams with echo cancellation, and provides a GPUI-global Audio mixer that plays and caches decoded sound-effect sources.
nodes.languageNotes: Audio is registered as a GPUI default-global mutated via update_default_global; device discovery runs on the background executor and publishes results into the AvailableAudioDevices global; echo cancellation is wired inline into the output source chain via inspect_buffer.

nodes.name: Audio
nodes.summary: GPUI-global audio mixer state holding the lazily-opened output stream, shared echo canceller, and a cache of decoded sound sources; exposes play_sound/end_call and lazy output-stream creation.

nodes.name: AudioDeviceInfo
nodes.summary: Descriptor pairing a device id with its rodio device description, with helpers to test whether the device matches a given id and supports input or output.

nodes.name: ensure_devices_initialized
nodes.summary: Lazily populates the AvailableAudioDevices GPUI global by spawning device enumeration on the background executor, then setting the global and refreshing the UI once discovery completes.

nodes.name: ensure_output_exists
nodes.summary: Lazily opens the output stream for the given device (attaching the echo canceller) if none exists yet, and returns a handle to the output mixer.

nodes.name: play_sound
nodes.summary: Resolves the configured output device from AudioSettings, ensures the output mixer exists, decodes/caches the sound source, and adds it to the mixer for playback.

nodes.name: sound_source
nodes.summary: Returns a buffered, decoded audio source for a Sound, loading the WAV asset via the GPUI asset source on a cache miss and memoizing the result in source_cache.

nodes.name: open_input_stream
nodes.summary: Builds a rodio microphone input stream for the given device id (or default), preferring 48kHz-family sample rates, mono-to-quad channel counts, and 512+ buffer sizes.

nodes.name: resolve_device
nodes.summary: Resolves a device id to a concrete rodio Device, falling back to the default host's default input or output device when no id is supplied.

nodes.name: open_output_stream
nodes.summary: Opens an output sink for the resolved device, seeds it with a silent keep-alive source, and inserts echo-cancellation processing into the mixed output buffer before it reaches the device.

nodes.name: get_available_audio_devices
nodes.summary: Enumerates all devices on the default host and collects them into AudioDeviceInfo descriptors, skipping any device whose id or description cannot be read.

nodes.name: audio_settings.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the AudioSettings GPUI settings struct holding the selected output and input device ids, derived from persisted settings content by parsing stored device-id strings.
nodes.languageNotes: from_settings parses optional persisted DeviceId strings via DeviceId::from_str, tolerating missing/invalid values by yielding None.

nodes.name: AudioSettings
nodes.summary: Settings struct exposing the user's chosen output and input audio device ids, constructed from persisted settings content via from_settings.

nodes.name: from_settings
nodes.summary: Constructs AudioSettings from persisted settings content, parsing the stored output and input device-id strings into DeviceId values and tolerating absent or unparseable entries.

nodes.name: auto_update_helper.rs
nodes.summary: Windows-specific auto-update helper bootstrapping dialog and performing application updates with messaging.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point initializing Windows error handling and delegating to platform implementation.

nodes.name: dialog.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Windows dialog UI for showing update progress and status with user interaction.

nodes.name: updater.rs
nodes.summary: Core update logic handling application termination, file replacement, and restart with error recovery.

nodes.name: channel.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the channel feature that wires up global initialization of the channel store and channel buffer subsystems.

nodes.name: channel_buffer.rs
nodes.summary: Implements ChannelBuffer, a collaborative shared-document buffer scoped to a channel that syncs edits and collaborator presence over the client protocol.

nodes.name: channel_store.rs
nodes.summary: Implements ChannelStore, the client-side cache and management API for channels (hierarchy, membership, notes, permissions) synchronized with the collaboration server.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a topologically-consistent channel tree model with membership sort keys and a GPUI global for app-wide access.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initializes the channel feature by calling channel_store::init and channel_buffer::init with the shared client and user store.

nodes.name: ChannelBuffer
nodes.summary: GPUI model representing a collaborative CRDT buffer tied to a channel, tracking collaborators, connection state and acknowledgment of remote edits.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a ChannelBuffer by subscribing to the channel's remote buffer and setting up collaborator/version tracking.

nodes.name: handle_update_channel_buffer
nodes.summary: Handles an incoming UpdateChannelBuffer protocol message by applying remote operations to the local buffer.

nodes.name: on_buffer_update
nodes.summary: Reacts to local buffer edit events by sending operations to collaborators and scheduling acknowledgment.

nodes.name: acknowledge_buffer_version
nodes.summary: Sends an acknowledgment of the current buffer version back to the collaboration server.

nodes.name: ChannelStore
nodes.summary: Central client-side store caching the user's channel tree, membership, and notes versions, exposing operations to create/rename/move/delete channels.

nodes.name: Channel
nodes.summary: Data model representing a single channel's identity, visibility and parent path within the channel hierarchy.

nodes.name: ChannelMembership
nodes.summary: Represents a user's membership record and role within a channel.

nodes.name: GlobalChannelStore
nodes.summary: GPUI global wrapper exposing the app-wide ChannelStore entity handle.

nodes.name: cloud_api_client.rs
nodes.summary: HTTP client for the Zed Cloud backend that manages user credentials, opens authenticated REST and WebSocket connections, and submits feedback and LLM token requests.

nodes.name: llm_token.rs
nodes.summary: Caches and refreshes the LLM API token obtained from the cloud backend behind a read-write lock, refetching on demand or on cache miss.

nodes.name: websocket.rs
nodes.summary: Wraps a WebSocket connection with a keepalive ping loop and channel-based send/receive interface spawned as a background task.

nodes.name: CloudApiClient
nodes.summary: Main client struct holding stored credentials and the shared HTTP client, providing methods to authenticate, connect, and call cloud endpoints.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the cloud collaboration endpoint using stored credentials.

nodes.name: send_authenticated_request
nodes.summary: Attaches credentials to a request builder, sends it via the HTTP client, and returns the raw response after checking status success.

nodes.name: validate_credentials
nodes.summary: Verifies a user_id/access_token pair against the cloud backend by calling the authenticated user endpoint directly.

nodes.name: build_request
nodes.summary: Adds content-type and Authorization headers to a request builder using the given credentials and finalizes the request body.

nodes.name: LlmApiToken
nodes.summary: Thread-safe cached wrapper around the current LLM API token, offering cached/refresh/clear operations backed by a CloudApiClient fetch.

nodes.name: cached
nodes.summary: Returns the cached LLM token if present, otherwise fetches a fresh one and populates the cache using an upgradable read lock.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Calls CloudApiClient::create_llm_token to obtain a fresh token and stores it in the write-locked cache.

nodes.name: Connection
nodes.summary: Represents an active WebSocket connection exposing async-channel based tx/rx handles to the background I/O task.

nodes.name: spawn
nodes.summary: Spawns a background task that drives the WebSocket connection, sending periodic keepalive pings and forwarding messages between the socket and channel endpoints.

nodes.name: cloud_llm_client.rs

nodes.name: predict_edits_v3.rs

nodes.name: predict_edits_v4.rs

nodes.name: UsageLimit

nodes.name: PredictEditsBody

nodes.name: CompletionBody

nodes.name: LanguageModel

nodes.name: CompletionEvent

nodes.name: PredictEditsV3Request
nodes.summary: Wraps a raw completion request as the v3 edit-prediction request payload.

nodes.name: PredictEditsV3Response
nodes.summary: Response from the v3 edit-prediction endpoint including output text, editable range, cursor offset and model version.

nodes.name: PredictEditsV4Request
nodes.summary: Request payload for the v4 edit-prediction endpoint.

nodes.name: PredictEditsV4Response
nodes.summary: Response payload for the v4 edit-prediction endpoint carrying a patch-based edit and model version instead of a raw excerpt.

nodes.name: mermaid_render.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root and public entrypoint for rendering Mermaid diagram source to themed SVG. Defines the MermaidTheme / AccentColor data model and the two-stage render_to_svg pipeline (merman render, then Zed-specific postprocess) used by the editor's markdown/diagram surfaces.
nodes.languageNotes: Rich module-level doc comment lays out design intent: color handling is layered across a merman config, accent-color CSS injection, and CSS rule injection. gpui is depended on only for the Hsla/Rgba color types.

nodes.name: MermaidTheme
nodes.summary: Public struct capturing every color and font knob the crate maps onto a Mermaid diagram (background, primary/secondary/tertiary, git branch palettes, ER row shading, actor/note/cluster colors, plus a Vec of derived accent colors). The primary extension point for matching diagrams to the host editor theme.

nodes.name: AccentColor
nodes.summary: Copy struct pairing a foreground and background Hsla, used to give individual diagram nodes accent colors derived from the Zed theme's player colors.

nodes.name: default
nodes.summary: Test-support Default impl for MermaidTheme, populating a light-mode Slate/Inter palette with concrete hex colors so tests and snapshots can render without a live editor theme. Gated behind test / test-support cfg.

nodes.name: css_color
nodes.summary: Converts an Hsla into a clamped 8-bit rgba() CSS color string. Shared helper that render.rs uses to serialize theme colors into merman config values.

nodes.name: render_to_svg
nodes.summary: Public entrypoint of the crate: renders Mermaid source to a raster-safe SVG via render::render_mermaid, then applies Zed theme and accent styling via postprocess::postprocess. The single API other crates call.

nodes.name: postprocess.rs
nodes.summary: Zed-specific SVG postprocessing stage that runs a chain of quick_xml event-iterator passes (strip_foreignobject, element_fixup, accent_colors, inject_css) over merman's raster-safe output to apply editor theme and accent styling in a single streaming parse.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Cow-backed quick_xml Events and per-pass Iterator adapters to transform the SVG without repeatedly reparsing or allocating new strings — a deliberate performance-vs-complexity tradeoff documented in the module header.

nodes.name: postprocess
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the postprocessing passes: extracts the SVG id, builds a lenient quick_xml reader iterator, threads it through strip_foreignobject/element_fixup/accent_colors/inject_css, and collects the transformed events back into a UTF-8 SVG string.

nodes.name: extract_svg_id
nodes.summary: Scans the SVG events for the root <svg> element and returns its id attribute (or an empty string), used to scope injected CSS rules to this specific diagram instance.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Iterator::next impl for ReaderIter, pulling owned quick_xml Events from the underlying reader and terminating cleanly on EOF so downstream passes can compose over a standard iterator.

nodes.name: render.rs
nodes.summary: First rendering stage: drives the merman HeadlessRenderer with a MermaidTheme-derived config and merman's resvg-safe SVG pipeline (foreignObject fallback, CSS override, !important stripping) to produce a rasterizer-safe SVG before Zed postprocessing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a static AtomicU64 counter to give each diagram a unique id, and opts into merman 0.6's raster-safe pipeline plus a CssOverridePostprocessor so host theme CSS wins in usvg/resvg.

nodes.name: render_mermaid
nodes.summary: Renders Mermaid source to a raster-safe SVG string synchronously: assigns a unique diagram id, builds the merman config from the theme, configures the resvg-safe pipeline with !important stripping, and runs the headless renderer.

nodes.name: to_merman_config
nodes.summary: Translates a MermaidTheme into a merman::MermaidConfig by serializing every theme color to a CSS string via css_color and assembling the themeVariables JSON, including per-branch git colors mapped into the config object. The core theme-to-engine mapping.

nodes.name: migrations.rs

nodes.name: migrate_settings

nodes.name: migrate_language_setting

nodes.name: migrator.rs

nodes.name: run_migrations

nodes.name: migrate_keymap

nodes.name: migrate_settings
nodes.summary: Entry point that runs the full chronological chain of settings.json migrations, spanning tree-sitter pattern rewrites and JSON value transforms.

nodes.name: migrate_edit_prediction_provider_settings
nodes.summary: Runs a single targeted tree-sitter migration that replaces the legacy edit_prediction_provider setting key.

nodes.name: MigrationType

nodes.name: patterns.rs
nodes.summary: Re-exports tree-sitter query pattern constants from the keymap and settings submodules for use by the migration engine.

nodes.name: notification_store.rs

nodes.name: NotificationEvent

nodes.name: NotificationEntry

nodes.name: NotificationSummary

nodes.name: load_more_notifications

nodes.name: splice_notifications

nodes.name: respond_to_notification

nodes.name: platform_title_bar.rs

nodes.name: ThemeSelection

nodes.name: IconThemeSelection

nodes.name: RemoteWorktree

nodes.name: Snapshot

nodes.name: File

nodes.name: clock.rs
nodes.summary: Implements distributed-systems clock primitives used for CRDT-style collaboration: a ReplicaId newtype, a Lamport logical clock, and a Global vector clock for tracking causal history across replicas.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements Ord/PartialOrd and a custom vector-clock join/meet (lattice) algebra typical of CRDT causality tracking.

nodes.summary: Newtype wrapper around a u16 identifying a collaboration replica (peer), with helpers for construction and detecting remote replicas.

nodes.name: Lamport
nodes.summary: Lamport logical clock combining a monotonically increasing value with a replica id, used to totally order events across replicas.

nodes.name: Global
nodes.summary: Vector clock tracking the latest observed Lamport timestamp per replica, with join/meet lattice operations and causal comparison methods (observed, changed_since).

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Merges another vector clock into self by taking the element-wise maximum, implementing the CRDT join (least upper bound) operation.

nodes.name: meet
nodes.summary: Computes the element-wise minimum with another vector clock and truncates trailing zeros, implementing the CRDT meet (greatest lower bound) operation.

nodes.name: observed_all
nodes.summary: Checks whether this vector clock has observed every timestamp recorded in another vector clock.

nodes.name: changed_since
nodes.summary: Determines whether any replica has advanced beyond the state recorded in another vector clock, used to detect new changes since a snapshot.

nodes.name: context.rs

nodes.name: entity_map.rs
nodes.summary: Implements GPUI's entity storage and reference-counting core: the slot-based EntityMap, strong/weak handles (Entity, WeakEntity, AnyEntity), leasing for exclusive access, and a leak detector.

nodes.name: headless_app_context.rs
nodes.summary: Provides HeadlessAppContext, an app runner without a real display used for offscreen rendering, screenshot capture, and clock-controlled headless execution.

nodes.name: test_app.rs
